what: literature sweep behind docs/plan/methodology_redesign.md, night of 2026-09-22/23: five search angles (web search plus arXiv abstracts, no full PDFs) and one synthesis against the record digest; claims of what a paper examines are from abstracts and method sections unless key_numbers says otherwise

systematic error discovery and auditing frameworks

papers.title: Failure detection in medical image classification under realistic distribution shifts: A large-scale benchmark
papers.authors_venue_year: Steinmetz, Frouin, Morard, Buvat; medRxiv preprint, May 2026
papers.rule: Grade confidence scoring functions across many tasks, backbones, training setups and failure sources with threshold-free risk-coverage metrics (AUGRC style); report that failure-detection performance is confounded with classifier accuracy, and test score aggregation (combining several CSFs) as a standing arm because no single CSF dominates.
papers.examines: Eight confidence scoring functions and two score-aggregation strategies on eight medical-imaging classification tasks under realistic shifts; graded by risk-coverage area metrics and silent-failure rate (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 8 CSFs, 2 aggregation strategies, 8 tasks; no single method dominates; aggregation matches or approaches the best single method and cuts silent failures; FD performance strongly correlated with accuracy (no numeric values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Largely covered: exp70/73/74 race the margin against many CSFs on 24 tasks x 16 encoders with E-AURC and AUGRC. Partial gap: the record only tests label-fitted fusion (exp65, +0.0006) and never a label-free rank/score aggregation of margin with a second cue; and the accuracy confound is addressed by excess AURC but not reported as a correlation across the 384 (task, encoder) cells.

papers.title: A Systematic Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Detection Under Representation and Training Paradigm Shifts
papers.authors_venue_year: Claros Olivares, Brockmeier; arXiv 2511.11934, Nov 2025 (rev. May 2026)
papers.rule: Rank detectors with a multiple-comparison-controlled rank pipeline over threshold-free metrics (AURC, AUGRC) and treat the winning detector family as a property of the representation, not of the score; simple probabilistic scores are the ones that catch misclassifications.
papers.examines: OOD and misclassification detectors across CNN/ViT, several training paradigms, four datasets with near/mid/far OOD; graded by AURC/AUGRC under rank tests with multiplicity control; Neural-Collapse statistics of the classifier predict which detector family wins (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 4 datasets (CIFAR-10/100, SuperCIFAR-100, TinyImageNet); margin/probabilistic scores best for misclassification; geometry-aware scores (NNGuide, fDBD, CTM) gain as shift grows; PCA filtering improves detectors (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Consistent with exp73 (margin beats kNN and Mahalanobis on all 24 tasks). Gap: the record runs one-sided sign tests per comparison without a family-wise control across the ~20 alternatives it has raced; and it never computes a representation statistic (e.g. Neural Collapse / class-mean separation on the cached embeddings) that would predict per-encoder which ranker wins.

papers.title: From Misclassifications to Outliers: Joint Reliability Assessment in Classification
papers.authors_venue_year: Li, Sha, Wang, Hospedales, Shen, Hu, Yu; arXiv 2603.03903, Mar 2026 (submitted to TPAMI)
papers.rule: Do not evaluate misclassification detection and OOD detection separately; grade a classifier's reliability jointly with double-scoring metrics (DS-F1, DS-AURC) that count both in-distribution errors and OOD inputs as failures to be rejected.
papers.examines: Joint reliability of classifiers on OpenOOD with a double scoring function (one score for OOD, one for ID error); graded by DS-F1 and DS-AURC (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: OOD-based scores give large gains under far-OOD, only marginal gains under near-OOD; SURE+ improves across scenarios (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Gap: the record's unit is an error under a labelled reference, so an out-of-support window (unseen class, sensor artefact) is either an error or ignored; there is no stratum of OOD windows and no DS-AURC-style joint grade. The cached embedding bank and the exported margin would allow a two-score evaluation without new training.

papers.title: Comparative Benchmarking of Failure Detection Methods in Medical Image Segmentation: Unveiling the Role of Confidence Aggregation
papers.authors_venue_year: Zenk, Zimmerer, Isensee, Traub, Norajitra, Jäger, Maier-Hein; arXiv 2406.03323, Jun 2024; Medical Image Analysis 2024
papers.rule: For segmentation, failure detection must be graded with risk-coverage analysis after an explicit, ablated aggregation of pixel confidences to the unit of decision; pairwise Dice between ensemble members is the baseline every new method must beat.
papers.examines: Failure-detection strategies (aggregations of pixel confidence, ensemble pairwise Dice, learned quality regressors) on five 3D medical datasets under test-time shift; graded by risk-coverage analysis (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 5 public 3D datasets; pairwise Dice of ensemble predictions is the robust baseline; aggregation choice decides the outcome (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Already covered: exp76 compares five window aggregators (gaps of order 0.001) and exp73 runs the 5-seed probe ensemble (mutual information, vote disagreement, bag margin) which loses 22/24. Cite as the origin of the aggregation rule the record already follows.

papers.title: ValUES: A Framework for Systematic Validation of Uncertainty Estimation in Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors_venue_year: Kahl, Lüth, Zenk, Maier-Hein, Jaeger; ICLR 2024 (oral); arXiv 2401.08501
papers.rule: Validate an uncertainty method by its downstream use (failure detection, OOD detection, active learning, calibration, ambiguity modelling), ablate the aggregation component separately from the score, and do not assume the aleatoric/epistemic split transfers from simulated to real data.
papers.examines: Uncertainty methods for segmentation in controlled environments with injected ambiguity and shift plus real data; graded on five downstream tasks with component ablations (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 5 downstream tasks; ensembles most robust, test-time augmentation a lightweight alternative; type separation works on simulation but not reliably on real data (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Partially followed: the record grades failure detection and the error-rate estimator, and ablates aggregation (exp76). Gap: no controlled-ambiguity environment (the record's exp23 reference disagreement is observational, not injected) and calibration of the margin is not graded alongside its ranking.

papers.title: Rethinking Evaluation Protocols of Visual Representations Learned via Self-supervised Learning
papers.authors_venue_year: Lee, Yoon, Ji, Kim, Hwang; arXiv 2304.03456, Apr 2023
papers.rule: Linear-probe and transfer results are very sensitive to probe hyperparameters; normalise probe inputs (batch norm before the linear layer) so that linear-probe and kNN rankings agree and evaluation is stable across learning rate, weight decay and schedule.
papers.examines: Sensitivity of linear probing, kNN and transfer learning of SSL representations to protocol hyperparameters; graded by stability of accuracy and by LP/kNN rank agreement (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Input batch normalisation considerably improves LP stability and resolves the kNN/LP inconsistency; SSL weight decay affects transferability invisibly to upstream LP/kNN (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Gap: the record reseeds the probe (exp79, 10 seeds) but does not vary learning rate, epochs or feature normalisation of Ai2's probe recipe, so it cannot say whether the margin's lead over controls survives a differently-normalised probe. Cheap to test on the cached embeddings: refit probes with standardised features and compare E-AURC of the margin.

papers.title: The Benchmark Lottery
papers.authors_venue_year: Dehghani, Tay, Gritsenko, Zhao, Houlsby, Diaz, Metzler, Vinyals; arXiv 2107.07002, Jul 2021
papers.rule: Which method looks superior is determined largely by which tasks are in the suite; a claim must state the task-selection rule and show how the ranking moves under alternative task subsets.
papers.examines: Ranking fragility across NLP, vision, IR, recommender and RL benchmarks as a function of task selection; graded by rank changes under subset choice (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: No numbers in abstract; the paper gives recommendations on mitigating the lottery.
papers.relation_to_record: Partially followed: the record fixes the suite at Ai2's 24 tasks and reports per-task wins, which limits cherry-picking. Gap: no leave-tasks-out or subset-resampling of the 24 tasks to show the margin's 24/24 or >=75% claim is not a property of Ai2's task mix (17 classification, 7 segmentation).

papers.title: GEO-Bench-2: From Performance to Capability, Rethinking Evaluation in Geospatial AI
papers.authors_venue_year: Simumba, Lehmann, Fraccaro, Alemohammad, De Mel, Khan, Maskey, Longepe, Zhu, Kerner, Bernabe-Moreno, Lacoste; arXiv 2511.15658, Nov 2025 (v2 Feb 2026)
papers.rule: Rank geospatial models within capability groups (datasets sharing resolution, bands, temporality) under a prescriptive adaptation protocol rather than by one aggregate score, because no single model dominates.
papers.examines: 19 permissively licensed datasets across classification, segmentation, regression, detection, instance segmentation; graded by capability-group rankings under a fixed protocol; seeds and hyperparameter budgets not stated in the abstract.
papers.key_numbers: 19 datasets, 5 task types; EO-pretrained models win on multispectral tasks, ImageNet models on high-resolution tasks; no single model dominates.
papers.relation_to_record: Partially followed: the record reports per-task and per-encoder results but aggregates by counting task wins, not by capability group. Gap: the 24 tasks could be grouped by sensor/resolution/temporality to state where the margin's lead is thin (many-class tasks are already flagged), which would follow the field's shift away from a single aggregate.

papers.title: Data-Centric Benchmark for Label Noise Estimation and Ranking in Remote Sensing Binary Building Segmentation
papers.authors_venue_year: Nogueira, Diaconu, Kerekes, Gawlikowski, Léonard, Ait Ali Braham, Goo, Zeng, Liu, Jain, Nascetti, Hänsch; arXiv 2603.00604, Feb 2026 (rev. Aug 2026), accepted Neurocomputing
papers.rule: Grade a label-noise ranker on a dataset with controlled, graded annotation perturbations so that the ranking of samples by noise severity can be scored against known injected noise; use uncertainty, prediction consistency and representation analysis as the candidate signals.
papers.examines: Methods that detect and rank training samples by label-noise severity in RS binary building segmentation; graded against controlled perturbations of a new public dataset (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Two proposed methods consistently beat baselines across settings (no values in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Gap: the record observes reference disagreement (exp23, WorldCover 2020 vs 2021) but never injects controlled reference noise into the grading labels to measure how E-AURC of the margin, the boundary claim, and exp78's error-rate estimate move with reference error rate. This is runnable on per-unit exports by flipping labels at set rates.

papers.title: Ground Truth in Classification Accuracy Assessment: Myth and Reality
papers.authors_venue_year: Foody; Geomatics 4(1), Feb 2024
papers.rule: Reference data are never perfect; accuracy assessment must state the reference error rate and, where possible, correct estimates of accuracy and class area for it, because bias grows with reference error and with class rarity.
papers.examines: Simulation of how ground-data error of varying magnitude and nature, interacting with class prevalence, biases per-class and overall accuracy and derived area estimates (search-result summary; abstract page returned 403).
papers.key_numbers: From the related Foody 2009/2010 work surfaced in the same search: 90%-accurate reference data made producer's accuracy of change read ~61% when the truth was 80%, and change extent 26% when the truth was 20%.
papers.relation_to_record: Partially followed: the record cites Olofsson 2014 and Stehman & Foody 2019 and treats WorldCover/LUCAS references as fallible. Gap: exp78's design-based error-rate estimator assumes the reviewer's labels are exact; no correction term or sensitivity band for reviewer error, and no statement of the reference error rate on the task cards.

papers.title: RSPDBench: Benchmarking Vision Foundation Models on Earth Observation Tasks Under Physically Grounded Remote-Sensing Product Degradations
papers.authors_venue_year: Faruk, Reza, Pallickara, Pallickara; arXiv 2609.23427, Sep 2026
papers.rule: Robustness must be measured as the drop from each model's clean baseline under physically grounded product degradations (spatial, radiometric, alignment, noise, harmonisation) and under compound chains, because compound chains expose failures that isolated degradations do not predict.
papers.examines: Seven foundation models and two supervised baselines on five EO datasets under audited primitive degradations and compound product chains; graded by performance drop from clean (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 5 datasets, 7 FMs + 2 supervised; compound-chain drops up to 38 percentage points beyond single degradations.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap: the record cites REOBench (known) and uses perturbations only as candidate signals (masking, tile phase, dihedral), never as an evaluation condition; whether the margin still ranks errors when the input product is degraded is unmeasured. Needs new encoder passes, so not runnable on cached embeddings.

papers.title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models for Agriculture Applications
papers.authors_venue_year: Shang, Das, Eldawy; arXiv 2606.29664, Jun 2026 (submitted to ACM SIGSPATIAL 2026)
papers.rule: Region-aware evaluation is a necessary standard: assign train, validation and test splits to disjoint regions so that reported numbers measure geographic transfer, and report per-class behaviour because models collapse to the frequent classes under regional shift.
papers.examines: Prithvi, SpectralGPT and SatMAE on multi-temporal crop segmentation and change detection across four US states with region-disjoint splits; graded by degradation under regional shift and rare-class recall (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 3 GFMs, 4 states; all three degrade sharply under regional shift and miss rare crops; input-format harmonisation affects each model differently.
papers.relation_to_record: Partially followed: the record inherits Ai2's splits (some are region-disjoint, some random) and does not state per task whether the test region overlaps training. Gap: the audit's headline (margin wins 24/24) is not stratified by split type, and the boundary/error claims are not reported per class frequency, although exp77 found scene-typicality confounded with class frequency.

field_rules: Grade a confidence ranker by threshold-free risk-coverage areas (AURC/E-AURC, AUGRC) across many tasks, backbones and failure sources, and never by a single fixed-threshold metric (Jaeger 2023, Traub 2024, Steinmetz 2026, Claros Olivares 2025).
Failure-detection scores are confounded with classifier accuracy; report excess or normalised metrics and the correlation with accuracy explicitly (Steinmetz 2026, Jaeger 2023).
When many rankers are compared, use a rank pipeline with multiple-comparison control, and expect the winning family to depend on the representation rather than the score (Claros Olivares 2025).
Misclassification and out-of-support inputs must be graded jointly; a selective system is scored on both with a double-scoring risk-coverage metric (Li 2026).
In segmentation, the aggregation from pixel confidence to the decision unit is a separately ablated component of the method, and ensemble pairwise Dice is the baseline to beat (Zenk 2024, Kahl 2024).

Uncertainty methods are validated by downstream use (failure detection, OOD, calibration, active learning) in controlled environments with injected ambiguity and shift, not by proxy scores alone (Kahl 2024).
Linear-probe results are hyperparameter-sensitive; normalise probe inputs and check that kNN and linear-probe rankings agree before drawing conclusions about the representation (Lee 2023).
A ranking claim must state the task-selection rule and show stability under task subsets, because the suite decides the winner (Dehghani 2021).
Geospatial model rankings are reported within capability groups (resolution, bands, temporality) under a prescriptive adaptation protocol, not as one aggregate (Simumba 2025).
Label-noise detectors are graded against controlled, graded annotation perturbations with known ground truth (Nogueira 2026).
Reference data are imperfect; state the reference error rate and correct or bound accuracy and area estimates for it, with bias rising for rare classes (Foody 2024).
Robustness is the drop from each model's clean baseline under physically grounded, compound product degradations, not generic corruptions (Faruk 2026).
Splits must be region-disjoint and results reported per class, because foundation models collapse to frequent classes under regional shift (Shang 2026).
gaps_in_our_tool: Multiplicity: the record runs one-sided sign tests per alternative across ~20 raced signals without family-wise control; Claros Olivares 2025 uses a multiple-comparison-controlled rank pipeline. Fix on existing per-task numbers.

Probe-protocol variance: exp79 covers seeds only; Lee 2023 shows learning rate, weight decay and feature normalisation move linear-probe results and that BN-on-inputs stabilises them. The margin's lead is untested under a standardised-feature probe; runnable on cached embeddings.
Joint OOD + error grading: the record has no out-of-support stratum and no DS-AURC-style metric (Li 2026); windows that are neither in the label space nor clean errors are invisible.

Task-subset stability: no leave-tasks-out or bootstrap over the 24 Ai2 tasks to show the 24/24 and >=75% claims are not a benchmark-lottery artefact (Dehghani 2021); nor capability-group reporting by sensor/resolution/temporality (Simumba 2025).

Reference-error sensitivity: exp23 observes reference disagreement but no controlled label-flip experiment measures how E-AURC, the boundary claim and exp78's error-rate estimate move with reference error rate (Nogueira 2026, Foody 2024); exp78 assumes reviewer labels are exact and gives no correction or band for reviewer error.

Accuracy confound reporting: excess AURC is used, but the correlation between the margin's failure-detection score and probe accuracy across the 384 task-encoder cells is not reported (Steinmetz 2026).
Label-free score aggregation: the field's standing arm is aggregating several confidence scores without labels (Steinmetz 2026); the record tests only label-fitted fusion (exp65).
Controlled-ambiguity validation and calibration: ValUES-style injected ambiguity/shift environments and a calibration grade of the margin alongside its ranking are absent (Kahl 2024).

Degradation as an evaluation condition: perturbations are used only as candidate signals; no measurement of the margin's ranking under physically grounded product degradations or compound chains (Faruk 2026); needs GPU passes.

Split-type and class-frequency stratification: the headline is not stratified by whether a task's split is region-disjoint, and error/boundary claims are not reported by class frequency despite exp77's confound (Shang 2026).

papers.title: Leveraging Unlabeled Data to Predict Out-of-Distribution Performance (ATC)
papers.authors_venue_year: Garg, Balakrishnan, Lipton, Neyshabur, Sedghi; ICLR 2022
papers.rule: Average Thresholded Confidence: fit one threshold on a labelled SOURCE (validation) set so that the fraction of source examples with confidence above it equals source accuracy; the target accuracy estimate is the fraction of unlabelled target examples whose confidence exceeds that threshold. Any confidence score (max-prob, margin, negative entropy) can be plugged in.
papers.examines: Dataset-level accuracy of a fixed classifier on shifted unlabelled test sets; graded by mean absolute error between estimated and true accuracy across synthetic corruptions, dataset reproductions and novel subpopulations.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: 2-4x lower estimation error than prior methods (DoC, GDE-style, importance weighting). Also proves that identifying accuracy is as hard as identifying the best predictor, so every estimator rests on an assumption about the shift.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. The record has the margin as an instance ranker and exp78's design-based estimate that needs labels on the deployment map; ATC would give a label-free point estimate of each task's error rate from the per-unit margin/p1 exports plus the probe's validation split. Not on the related-work page (2201.04234 absent).

papers.title: Predicting with Confidence on Unseen Distributions (DoC)
papers.authors_venue_year: Guillory, Shankar, Ebrahimi, Darrell, Schmidt; ICCV 2021
papers.rule: Difference of Confidences: the drop in mean top-1 confidence from source to target predicts the drop in accuracy, optionally with a linear map fitted on held-out shifts; distributional distances (Frechet, MMD) between feature sets do not.
papers.examines: Dataset-level accuracy under natural shifts (ImageNet-V2, -R, -Vid-Robust, etc.); graded by error of predicted accuracy against true accuracy.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: 46% lower predictive error than distance-based baselines on realistic shifts.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, and a direct methodological contrast: the record tested feature-space typicality (kNN, Mahalanobis, SHRUG-FM U_E) as instance rankers and they lost; DoC is the dataset-level analogue of that finding (confidence beats distance) and is the cheapest estimator to grade on 24x16 from mean p1 per task.

papers.title: Agreement-on-the-Line: Predicting the Performance of Neural Networks under Distribution Shift
papers.authors_venue_year: Baek, Jiang, Raghunathan, Kolter; NeurIPS 2022
papers.rule: When ID and OOD accuracy are linearly related across a family of models (accuracy-on-the-line), pairwise ID vs OOD AGREEMENT of those models lies on a line with the same slope and intercept; agreement needs no labels, so the OOD accuracy line can be fitted from unlabelled OOD data alone (ALine-S/ALine-D estimators).
papers.examines: Dataset-level OOD accuracy across a model family; graded by MAE of predicted accuracy and by whether the linear fit holds (R^2 across models).
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: outperforms prior estimators even where the line breaks; the phenomenon is reported to hold only for neural-network classifiers.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. exp73 used seed ensembles only as an instance ranker; the 16 encoders and 10 seeds per task (exp79) form exactly the model family this method needs, provided the tool has at least one genuinely shifted unlabelled split per task (geographic or temporal), which the Ai2 splits may not give.

papers.title: Predicting the Performance of Foundation Models via Agreement-on-the-Line
papers.authors_venue_year: Saxena, Kim, Mehra, Baek, Kolter, Raghunathan; arXiv 2404.01542, 2024 (v2 Oct 2024; NeurIPS 2024 per listing, from abstract page only)
papers.rule: For lightly finetuned or probed foundation models, agreement-on-the-line holds only when ensemble members differ by RANDOM HEAD INITIALISATION; varying data order or subsets gives too little diversity. Ensembles of different foundation models finetuned on the same task also lie on the line.
papers.examines: Dataset-level OOD accuracy prediction for finetuned/probed foundation models across vision and language shifts; graded by MAE of predicted accuracy and linear-fit quality.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: no numbers in the abstract; the claim is which randomness source induces the line.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap that matches the record's assets precisely: 10 seeds x 16 encoders of linear probes on frozen encoders are the two ensemble types the paper says work. Needs per-seed decisions exported (digest says cheap follow-up).

papers.title: Characterizing Out-of-Distribution Error via Optimal Transport (COT / COTT)
papers.authors_venue_year: Lu, Qin, Zhai, Shen, Chen, Wang, Kolouri, Stepputtis, Campbell, Sycara; NeurIPS 2023
papers.rule: Confidence-based estimators UNDERESTIMATE error when the predicted label marginal on the target drifts from the true one (pseudo-label shift); estimate error as the optimal-transport cost between the target softmax outputs and the source label marginal (COT), or threshold the transport cost per sample (COTT).
papers.examines: Dataset-level OOD error; graded by MAE against true error and specifically by the underestimation bias of ATC/DoC-style methods under label shift.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: up to 3x lower estimation error than prior state of the art.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. Names the failure mode most relevant to EO maps (class prevalence differs by region and date); needs full per-unit probability vectors, obtainable from cached embeddings + the probe on CPU.

papers.title: Confidence and Dispersity Speak: Characterising Prediction Matrix for Unsupervised Accuracy Estimation (nuclear norm)
papers.authors_venue_year: Deng, Suh, Gould, Zheng; ICML 2023 (arXiv 2302.01094)
papers.rule: A well-performing model on a test set gives predictions that are both confident (peaked rows) and dispersed across classes (balanced columns); the nuclear norm of the softmax prediction matrix captures both and correlates with accuracy across shifts. Known limit: severe class imbalance breaks the dispersity assumption.
papers.examines: Dataset-level accuracy across shifts and architectures (ViT, ConvNeXt; ImageNet, CUB); graded by correlation (R^2, rho) between the score and true accuracy across shifted test sets.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: improved correlation and robustness over prior methods; imbalance stated as a limitation.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, with a warning: EO segmentation tasks are heavily imbalanced (flood/no-flood), which is the paper's own stated failure mode; the tool's per-class recording would expose it.

papers.title: MaNo: Exploiting Matrix Norm for Unsupervised Accuracy Estimation Under Distribution Shifts
papers.authors_venue_year: Xie, Odonnat, Feofanov, Deng, Zhang, An; NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv 2405.18979)
papers.rule: Logit-based estimators are biased by overconfidence under natural shift; apply a data-dependent normalisation to the logits (softrun) and use the Lp norm of the normalised logit matrix as the accuracy score, justified by a low-density-separation argument.
papers.examines: Dataset-level accuracy across synthetic, natural and subpopulation shifts; graded by correlation with true accuracy across test sets.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: state-of-the-art across architectures; no numbers in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap; same inputs as the nuclear norm (logit matrix from embeddings + probe). Together with Deng 2023 and GdScore it is the family the field grades new dataset-level estimators against.

papers.title: Leveraging Gradients for Unsupervised Accuracy Estimation under Distribution Shift (GdScore)
papers.authors_venue_year: Xie, Odonnat, Feofanov, Redko, Zhang, An; TMLR 2025 (arXiv 2401.08909)
papers.rule: The norm of the classification-layer gradient of the cross-entropy loss against the model's own pseudo-labels, after one step over the unlabelled test set, is larger when the model generalises worse; it replaces ProjNorm's retraining (Yu 2022, arXiv 2202.05834) with one gradient step on the head.
papers.examines: Dataset-level accuracy under shift; graded by linear correlation with true accuracy, with the claim that the relation stays linear at high error where confidence-based scores saturate.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: significantly outperforms prior estimators across architectures and shifts.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap; for a linear probe the head gradient is a closed form of embeddings and softmax outputs, so it is computable from the cached bank without encoder passes.

papers.title: Label-free estimation of clinically relevant performance metrics under distribution shifts
papers.authors_venue_year: Fluehmann, Bissoto, Hoang, Koch; UNSURE 2025 workshop at MICCAI (oral); arXiv 2507.22776
papers.rule: Generalise ATC/DoC-style estimators to estimate the full CONFUSION MATRIX rather than accuracy, so that per-class metrics (sensitivity, specificity, counts) follow; grade estimators separately under real-world shift, covariate shift and PREVALENCE shift, because simulated prevalence shift makes all confidence-based estimators fail systematically.
papers.examines: Dataset-level confusion matrix and derived metrics of chest X-ray classifiers under real and simulated shifts; graded by error of estimated vs true metric per shift type.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: outperforms baselines for real-world and covariate shifts; systematic failure of every method under simulated prevalence shifts.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap and the honest framing the task asks for: a label-free estimate exists, its known failure mode is prevalence shift, and the confusion-matrix form is what an EO map user needs (per-class omission/commission, cf. Olofsson 2014 already cited).

papers.title: ConfIC-RCA: Statistically Grounded Efficient Estimation of Segmentation Quality (In-Context Reverse Classification Accuracy)
papers.authors_venue_year: Cosarinsky, Billot, Mansilla, Jimenez, Gaggion, Fu, Tirer, Ferrante; IEEE TMI 2025 (arXiv 2503.04522)
papers.rule: Reverse Classification Accuracy: treat the predicted mask as pseudo ground truth, use it to segment (via an in-context segmenter with retrieved references) a small labelled reference set, and read the best Dice on the references as the quality of the predicted mask; wrap it in split conformal prediction to give per-image quality INTERVALS with coverage guarantees instead of point estimates.
papers.examines: Per-image segmentation quality (Dice) without a label for that image; graded on 10 medical segmentation tasks by correlation with true Dice and by conformal coverage of the intervals.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: validated on 10 tasks across organs and modalities; no numbers in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap in method: the record has no per-map quality estimator for segmentation and no conformal interval around a label-free estimate; RCA needs a small labelled reference set (allowed by filter 2) and an in-context segmenter, not the frozen probe.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Test-Time Adaptation: Style Invariance as a Correctness Likelihood (SICL)
papers.authors_venue_year: Nam, Kim, Jeong, Yang; WACV 2026 (arXiv 2512.07390)
papers.rule: Instance-wise correctness likelihood = prediction consistency of the model across style-altered variants of the input (forward passes only), used to recalibrate confidence under test-time adaptation.
papers.examines: Instance-level calibration of adapted classifiers; graded by expected calibration error across four baselines, five TTA methods, three architectures, two scenarios.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: mean 13 percentage-point reduction in calibration error.
papers.relation_to_record: Already covered in substance: the record tested tile-phase/perturbation stability, dihedral consistency, masking perturbation and shift-TTA of the head (exp53) as instance rankers and they lost to the margin. Cite only as the 2026 confirmation that the field grades consistency by calibration, not ranking; a new encoder pass per variant would be needed.

papers.title: Right Regions, Wrong Labels: Semantic Label Flips in Segmentation under Correlation Shift
papers.authors_venue_year: Achara, Yahathugoda, Byrne, Antonelli, Puyol Anton, Hammers, King; arXiv 2604.13326, CAO workshop at ICLR 2026
papers.rule: Decompose segmentation foreground error into correct, identity-flipped (right region, wrong foreground class) and missed-to-background pixels; a label-free 'flip-risk' score from the entropy over FOREGROUND classes only flags identity flips at inference, which grow as category-scene correlation in training increases.
papers.examines: Pixel-level error types of segmentation models under correlation shift; graded by the Flip metric against ground truth and by how flip-risk ranks flipped pixels.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract only: no numbers in the abstract; the claim is that the gap between common and rare scene conditions widens with correlation strength.
papers.relation_to_record: Partly covered (exp76 compared confidence forms; exp77 tested scene-typicality) but the error TYPE decomposition is absent: the record reports boundary vs interior errors, not identity flips vs omissions, and the tool's explain module could carry this label-free cue on multi-class tasks.

field_rules: A label-free accuracy estimate is graded by the absolute error between estimated and true accuracy across many (model, shifted test set) pairs, never on one dataset, because identifying accuracy is as hard as identifying the best predictor and every estimator carries a shift assumption (Garg et al. 2022, ATC).

Confidence-based estimators must be fitted on a labelled source split (a threshold or a linear map) and applied to unlabelled targets; feature-distribution distances are not a substitute (Guillory et al. 2021, DoC; Garg et al. 2022).

When a family of models is available, unlabelled pairwise agreement on the target replaces labels: ID-vs-OOD agreement lies on the same line as accuracy, and for probed foundation models the family must differ by random head initialisation (Baek et al. 2022; Saxena et al. 2024).

Every confidence-based estimator underestimates error when the predicted class marginal on the target differs from the source label marginal; the fix is an optimal-transport cost to the source marginal, and the grade must include label/prevalence-shift cases (Lu et al. 2023, COT/COTT).

Dataset-level scores are compared by correlation with true accuracy across shifted sets, and the ones that survive are logit-matrix statistics with an overconfidence correction (nuclear norm, Deng et al. 2023; MaNo, Xie et al. 2024) or the one-step head-gradient norm (GdScore, Xie et al. 2025), with class imbalance as a declared failure mode (Deng et al. 2023).

Estimate the confusion matrix, not accuracy, when users need per-class metrics, and report estimator behaviour separately under covariate shift and prevalence shift, where all confidence-based estimators fail (Fluehmann et al. 2025).

Per-image segmentation quality without a label is estimated by reverse classification against a small labelled reference set and reported as a conformal interval with coverage, not a point (Cosarinsky et al. 2025, ConfIC-RCA).

Instance-level consistency under semantics-preserving perturbation is graded as a correctness likelihood by calibration error (Nam et al. 2026, SICL), and segmentation error is decomposed into region, identity-flip and omission components before any label-free flag is judged (Achara et al. 2026).
gaps_in_our_tool: The tool says 'how wrong the map is needs a reference'; the field has label-free dataset-level estimators with a declared failure mode (prevalence/pseudo-label shift: Lu 2023, Fluehmann 2025). Gap: no ATC/DoC/COT estimate is computed, though the per-unit exports (margin, p1, decision) and the probe validation split are enough for ATC and DoC on 24x16 tonight; COT, nuclear norm, MaNo and GdScore need full probability vectors from the cached embeddings + probe (CPU per encoder).

Grading rule not followed: the field grades an estimator by MAE across many (model, test set) pairs including shifted ones (Garg 2022). The 24 Ai2 tasks are mostly in-distribution splits; grading on 24x16 would measure in-distribution bias only unless a geographic/temporal held-out split per task is defined, which the record does not have.

Agreement-on-the-line is untested although the record holds the exact family it needs (10 random-init probe seeds x 16 encoders; Saxena 2024 says random head init is the diversity that works). exp73 used seed disagreement only as an instance ranker; GDE (Jiang 2022, cited) as a dataset-level error-rate estimate is also not on the record. Needs per-seed decisions exported.

Class-prevalence shift is the named failure mode of every confidence-based estimator (Lu 2023, Fluehmann 2025) and EO maps shift prevalence by region and date (flood extent, crop mix); the tool's estimate module has no label-free component and no prevalence-shift check at all.

The estimate module reports overall error with a labelled sample; the field's clinical line estimates the full confusion matrix (Fluehmann 2025), which for maps is the per-class omission/commission that Olofsson 2014 (cited) requires. A label-free confusion-matrix estimate could serve as the predictor in the difference/PPI estimator already shipped, reducing the labelled sample needed.

No per-map segmentation quality estimate or interval exists; the field's answer for segmentation is reverse classification accuracy against a small reference set with conformal intervals (Cosarinsky 2025). Not computable from the frozen probe; would need a reference set per task and an in-context segmenter.

Segmentation error is not decomposed into identity flips vs omissions (Achara 2026); the record's boundary-vs-interior split is a different axis, and the explain module has no flip-risk cue for multi-class tasks.

Label-free model selection across the 16 encoders (which encoder to deploy on an unlabelled region) is not offered; the field does it by agreement (Saxena 2024) and by pseudo-label discrepancy (Larrea et al. 2026, arXiv 2608.25810, AURCC, Spearman up to 0.943 over six models).

papers.title: PPI++: Efficient Prediction-Powered Inference
papers.authors_venue_year: Angelopoulos, Duchi, Zrnic; arXiv 2311.01453 (Nov 2023, rev. Mar 2024); a search result says it appears in Annals of Applied Statistics 2026
papers.rule: Estimate with the difference estimator but multiply the prediction term by a power-tuning coefficient lambda chosen from the data to minimise variance; lambda=0 recovers the classical labelled-only estimate, lambda=1 is plain PPI, so the tuned interval is never wider than the classical one (abstract plus method summary).
papers.examines: Estimation of means, quantiles and M-estimation parameters from a small labelled set plus a large predicted set; graded by confidence-interval width at nominal coverage.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract gives no numbers; the claim is that intervals 'always improve on classical intervals using only the labeled data'.
papers.relation_to_record: Extends the plain PPI already cited and the 'PPI = difference estimator' equivalence (Mozer 2026). exp78 ran a difference estimator with confidence as predictor as one arm, apparently with the coefficient fixed at 1; the field's rule is to tune lambda (PPI++) so the arm cannot lose to the stratified classical estimator. Testable on exp78's per-unit files.

papers.title: Active Statistical Inference
papers.authors_venue_year: Zrnic, Candès; ICML 2024 (arXiv 2403.03208, rev. Apr 2026)
papers.rule: Under a label budget, sample each unit for labelling with a probability that increases with the model's uncertainty, then form an inverse-probability-weighted prediction-powered estimator; valid intervals for any black-box model and any distribution (abstract).
papers.examines: Mean and regression-coefficient estimation with model-chosen labelling; graded by interval width and test power versus non-adaptive designs on public-opinion, census and proteomics data.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract: 'same level of accuracy with far fewer samples' than baselines; no figure in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. The tool's design is a fixed confidence-quintile Neyman allocation; active inference is the field's version of 'let the margin choose who gets labelled' with a design-consistent estimator. It can be simulated on the fully labelled per-unit exports (24 tasks x 16 encoders) with no GPU.

papers.title: Robust Sampling for Active Statistical Inference
papers.authors_venue_year: Li, Zrnic, Candès; NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2511.08991)
papers.rule: Because inaccurate uncertainty scores can make active sampling noisier than uniform sampling, mix the uncertainty-driven sampling rule with uniform sampling and calibrate the mixture so the estimator is never worse than uniform and better when the scores are good (abstract).
papers.examines: Failure mode of active inference under miscalibrated uncertainty; graded by estimator variance and coverage on social-science and survey data.
papers.key_numbers: None in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, and directly relevant: the record shows the margin's ranking quality varies across 16 encoders and 24 tasks, so any confidence-driven label allocation needs the field's hedge against a poorly ranked task. Monte Carlo on the per-unit exports would grade it.

papers.title: Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference for Hybrid Language Model Evaluation
papers.authors_venue_year: Fisch, Maynez, Hofer, Dhingra, Globerson, Cohen; NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv 2406.04291)
papers.rule: Partition units into strata where the automatic rater's accuracy differs, draw labels by stratified sampling, and apply PPI with a separate power-tuning coefficient per stratum; valid without assumptions on the rater (abstract plus method summary).
papers.examines: Hybrid human/auto evaluation of language-model outputs; graded by confidence-interval width at nominal coverage.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract: 'substantially tighter confidence intervals than unstratified approaches' when rater accuracy varies across strata; no figure.
papers.relation_to_record: Closest published relative of exp78's confidence-stratified design. The tool stratifies and uses classical within-stratum estimation; StratPPI adds per-stratum tuned use of the predictions on the unlabelled units. A gap in the estimator, not the design.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Inference with Imputed Covariates and Nonuniform Sampling
papers.authors_venue_year: Kluger, Lu, Zrnic, Wang, Bates; arXiv 2501.18577 (Jan 2025, rev. Nov 2025)
papers.rule: When the labelled units come from a weighted, stratified or clustered sample, or when features as well as labels are imputed, use bootstrap confidence intervals for the predict-then-debias estimator; valid under no assumption on model quality (abstract).
papers.examines: Validity of PPI intervals under survey-type sampling designs; graded by coverage in simulation and applications.
papers.key_numbers: None in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. The tool's ratio estimator for tile clusters (design effect 1.2-3) is classical; this paper is the PPI-side treatment of exactly that clustered/stratified case, so a PPI arm on segmentation tiles must use these intervals rather than i.i.d. PPI formulas.

papers.title: Regression coefficient estimation from remote sensing maps
papers.authors_venue_year: Lu, Kluger, Bates, Wang; arXiv 2407.13659 (Jul 2024, rev. Jul 2025); Remote Sensing of Environment 2025 (search result)
papers.rule: Treat an ML-derived map as an auxiliary variable and use a small random ground-truth sample to debias downstream estimates via PPI, with no assumptions on the map's error structure (abstract).
papers.examines: Bias of regression coefficients computed from remote-sensing map products; graded by interval coverage and effective sample size versus ground-truth-only estimation.
papers.key_numbers: Effective sample size gains of up to 17x over ground-truth-only (abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Already in spirit via 'Angelopoulos PPI 2023' and Mozer 2026, but this is the canonical EO application and is not on the cited-id list. Useful as the anchor for saying what a map user expects when the map feeds a downstream regression, which the tool does not address.

papers.title: Conformal Risk Control
papers.authors_venue_year: Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, Schuster; ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2208.02814, rev. Jun 2025). Companion: Learn then Test, Angelopoulos, Bates, Candès, Jordan, Lei, Annals of Applied Statistics 2025 (arXiv 2110.01052)
papers.rule: For any loss that is monotone in a threshold (e.g. false-negative rate of a segmentation mask as the threshold on pixel scores is lowered), pick the threshold on a calibration sample so that the expected loss on new data is at most alpha, tight to O(1/n); Learn then Test does the same for non-monotone losses by multiple hypothesis testing (abstracts).
papers.examines: Post-hoc calibration of set-valued outputs (segmentation masks, multilabel sets) to a risk level; graded by realised risk versus alpha on held-out data.
papers.key_numbers: Guarantee tight up to O(1/n); applications include false-negative-rate control in vision and token-level F1 in NLP (abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. The record answers 'how wrong is the map' as an estimate with an interval; the field also answers 'how much to review or dilate so the missed-error rate is at most alpha' as a risk-control threshold on the margin. Computable from the per-unit exports with a labelled calibration split.

papers.title: A Framework for Efficient Model Evaluation through Stratification, Sampling, and Estimation
papers.authors_venue_year: Fogliato, Patil, Monfort, Perona; ECCV 2024
papers.rule: To estimate a model's accuracy under a label budget, stratify by k-means clustering on a prediction of per-unit model performance (not on raw confidence bins), allocate one-shot, and use model-assisted estimators that exploit predicted accuracy on the unlabelled units; abstract and introduction read.
papers.examines: Precision of accuracy estimates for computer-vision models across stratification, sampling and estimator choices; graded by variance versus simple random sampling.
papers.key_numbers: Up to 10x efficiency gain over simple random sampling; model-assisted estimators generally more efficient than labelled-only (abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Contradicts one tool choice: the tool cuts strata at confidence quintiles; this paper's key result is that strata formed by k-means on a predicted-performance score are more efficient. Cheap to test on exp78's per-unit files (quintile vs k-means on the margin or on a fitted error predictor).

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Active Testing
papers.authors_venue_year: Ashouritaklimi, Kilian, Huang, Rainforth, Caron; arXiv 2607.08347 (Jul 2026)
papers.rule: Estimate a model's risk under a label budget by combining active-testing acquisition (which test points to label) with prediction-powered control variates that residualise the loss, keeping unbiasedness while cutting variance; asymptotic normality gives intervals (abstract).
papers.examines: Label-efficient test-risk estimation on tabular regression and image classification; graded by interval coverage and width against labels used.
papers.key_numbers: Abstract: target coverage reached 'with substantially fewer labels and smaller widths'; no figure.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. Same question as exp78 ('how wrong is this model at budget B') answered with sequential acquisition plus control variates instead of a fixed stratified design. Abstract only; method details not read.

papers.title: Choosing a sample size allocation to strata based on trade-offs in precision when estimating accuracy and area of a rare class from a stratified sample
papers.authors_venue_year: Stehman, Wagner; Remote Sensing of Environment 2023 (Nov 2023)
papers.rule: Sample allocation to strata trades precision among user's accuracy, producer's accuracy and area; the trade-off grows as the target class becomes rarer (<=10% of the region) and user's accuracy is the estimate most sensitive to the allocation, so an allocation must be chosen against all three targets, not one (search-result abstract only; the page returned 403).
papers.examines: Precision of UA, PA and area estimates under different allocations for a rare binary target class (change, forest loss, water, burned area).
papers.key_numbers: Target class rare at <=10% of the study region; no other figures in the abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap in what the tool reports: exp78 estimates an error rate with Neyman allocation for that single target; the map-accuracy field expects per-class user's/producer's accuracy and error-adjusted area, and shows Neyman for one target degrades the others. Per-unit exports (decision, error, class) allow computing all three.

papers.title: Land Cover and Change Map Accuracy Assessment and Area Estimation Good Practices Protocol, Version 1.1
papers.authors_venue_year: Tyukavina, Stehman, Foody, Bontemps, See, Olofsson, Tsendbazar, et al.; CEOS WGCV Land Product Validation subgroup, November 2025, doi:10.5067/doc/ceoswgcv/lpv/lc.001
papers.rule: Accuracy assessment is a probability sample of independent reference data with design-based estimators (overall, user's, producer's accuracy and class area from the reference sample, never from pixel counting); algorithm-variance metrics are not an accuracy assessment; at least 30% of budget goes to assessment; model-assisted estimators (post-stratification, regression, logistic) may use a wall-to-wall map or continuous layer as auxiliary while keeping design-based validity; local map quality metrics are expected to supplement global ones (executive summary and chapters 3 and 5 read from the PDF text).
papers.examines: Community standard for what a map producer must report and how; graded by conformance to the sampling, response and analysis design elements listed in its tables.
papers.key_numbers: Budget: at least 30% of the mapping project for assessment; UA objective: 75-150 units per map-class stratum; Neyman optimal allocation preferred for overall accuracy or change area with two strata (Stehman 2012 cited).
papers.relation_to_record: Olofsson 2014 and Stehman & Foody 2019 are cited; this 2025 protocol supersedes them as the field standard and states explicitly that a confidence layer alone is not an accuracy assessment, which frames the tool's `estimate` command as the compliant half and its rankers as the non-compliant half. It names model-assisted estimation with a continuous auxiliary (the margin qualifies) as good practice.

papers.title: Optimizing satellite-based cropland area estimation through integrated map accuracy assessment and stratified sampling design across six African countries
papers.authors_venue_year: Adebayo, Nakalembe, Skakun, Frimpong, et al.; International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 2026
papers.rule: Link a map's user's/producer's accuracy to the relative efficiency of a map-stratified design and pick the map (stratifier) and sample size that reach a target coefficient of variation; a companion 2025 RSE paper (S0034425725002093) finds producer's accuracy drives relative efficiency more than user's accuracy (search-result abstracts only; both pages returned 403).
papers.examines: Sample-based cropland area estimation with seven land-cover products as strata in Kenya, Rwanda, Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia; graded by precision (CV) and required sample size.
papers.key_numbers: 8-15% precision versus 27-36% for conventional methods; most efficient stratifiers cut required sample size 20-40% at a 10% CV target.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap in planning: exp78 grades coverage and bias at a given budget, but the field's design question is inverted, 'what n reaches a target CV given this map's PA/UA'. The tool has no sample-size planner; the relative-efficiency-vs-accuracy relation could be fitted on the 24 fully labelled tasks.

field_rules: Never estimate a population quantity from predictions alone; use a probability sample of reference labels and treat the model output as an auxiliary variable whose only job is variance reduction, with validity coming from the design (CEOS LPV protocol 2025; Lu et al. 2024/2025).

Use the predictions on the unlabelled units through a debiased (difference/PPI) estimator with a data-tuned coefficient so the interval can never be wider than the labelled-only one (PPI++, Angelopoulos, Duchi, Zrnic 2023).
When the model's accuracy varies across identifiable groups, stratify and tune the prediction weight per stratum (StratPPI, Fisch et al. 2024).

If the model's uncertainty may choose which units get labelled, weight by the inclusion probabilities and hedge the uncertainty-driven rule with a uniform component so a badly ranked case is never worse than random (Active Statistical Inference, Zrnic & Candès 2024; Robust Sampling, Li, Zrnic, Candès 2025).
For clustered or stratified labelled samples and imputed covariates, PPI intervals must come from a design-aware bootstrap, not i.i.d. formulas (Kluger et al. 2025).

Strata for accuracy estimation are best formed by clustering a predicted per-unit performance score rather than by fixed confidence bins, and model-assisted estimators beat labelled-only ones (Fogliato et al., ECCV 2024).

A map user is owed user's accuracy, producer's accuracy and error-adjusted area per class with standard errors, and an allocation chosen for one of these degrades the others, most of all user's accuracy of a rare class (Stehman & Wagner 2023; CEOS protocol 2025).

Sample size is planned backwards from a target coefficient of variation using the map's producer's and user's accuracy, which set the design's relative efficiency (Adebayo et al. 2026; RSE 2025 companion).

Beyond point estimates with intervals, a deployable guarantee is a threshold chosen so a monotone risk such as the missed-error rate is at most alpha on new data (Conformal Risk Control, Angelopoulos et al. 2024; Learn then Test 2025).

Label-efficient risk estimation can be sequential: acquire the next label where it most reduces variance and residualise the loss with prediction-based control variates while staying unbiased (Prediction-Powered Active Testing, 2026).
gaps_in_our_tool: The difference-estimator arm in exp78 fixes the prediction coefficient at 1; the field tunes it (PPI++), which is the rule that makes the arm provably no worse than the stratified classical estimator, and StratPPI tunes it per confidence stratum. Both are computable on exp78's per-unit files.

The design is one-shot fixed Neyman on confidence quintiles; the field's alternative is active inference where the margin sets inclusion probabilities, with the Li-Zrnic-Candès uniform mixture as the guard for tasks where the margin ranks poorly. The record's own finding that ranking quality varies by task and encoder is the reason the guard matters; Monte Carlo on the 24 fully labelled tasks would grade it.

Strata are confidence quintiles; Fogliato et al. (ECCV 2024) report that k-means strata on a predicted-performance score are more efficient, up to 10x over SRS. The tool has not compared quintile cuts against clustered cuts.

The tile-cluster ratio estimator has classical intervals only; if a PPI-style arm is used on segmentation tiles, its intervals must be the design-aware bootstrap of Kluger et al. 2025, which the tool lacks.

The tool reports an error rate; the map-accuracy field (CEOS 2025, Stehman & Wagner 2023) expects per-class user's accuracy, producer's accuracy and error-adjusted area with standard errors, and warns that Neyman for one target harms the others. The per-unit exports carry decision, error and class, so these can be added without new labels.
No sample-size planner: the field plans n backwards from a target CV using PA/UA-driven relative efficiency (Adebayo 2026; RSE 2025); the tool only grades a given budget.

No risk-control output: Conformal Risk Control / Learn then Test would turn the margin into a threshold with a guaranteed bound on the missed-error rate at review budget B, a different deliverable from an estimate with an interval, and it is computable from the per-unit exports with a labelled calibration split.

The CEOS 2025 protocol states that algorithm-variance or confidence layers are not an accuracy assessment; the tool's docs should say plainly that only `sample`/`estimate` produce an accuracy assessment in the protocol's sense and that the rankers are review-ordering aids.

No sequential option: Prediction-Powered Active Testing (2026) and the UCB allocation of Ye, Lyu, Tao (2604.12497, 68-task survey, uniform's 10-12% gap cut to 2-6%) show that spending the budget in rounds approaches the Neyman oracle without the pilot estimates the fixed design needs.

papers.title: RSPDBench: Benchmarking Vision Foundation Models on Earth Observation Tasks Under Physically Grounded Remote-Sensing Product Degradations
papers.authors_venue_year: Tanjim Bin Faruk, Khondaker Masfiq Reza, Shrideep Pallickara, Sangmi Lee Pallickara; arXiv, 20 Sep 2026
papers.rule: Evaluate a frozen encoder with a head trained on clean data, then report robustness as the drop from that model's OWN clean baseline (native protocol), under four primitive product degradations (effective-resolution loss, radiometric gain shift, band misregistration, signal-relative sensor noise) AND compound product chains, because compound chains fail in ways the isolated primitives do not predict.
papers.examines: Inference of 7 foundation-model entries plus 2 supervised baselines on 5 EO datasets under physically grounded product defects; graded by accuracy drop from each model's clean baseline (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Compound degradation chains drop performance up to 38 percentage points beyond the strongest single component; resolution-conditioned and channel-grouped encoders protect different failure axes.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. Lehmann 2026 (2608.16614, known) covers calibration drift under cloud/noise; RSPDBench adds product-level defects (misregistration, radiometric gain, compound chains) and the native-baseline rule. The tool never grades whether the margin's ranking survives product degradation; that would need re-encoding, not cached embeddings.

papers.title: Distribution Shifts at Scale: Out-of-distribution Detection in Earth Observation (TARDIS)
papers.authors_venue_year: Burak Ekim, Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, Caleb Robinson, Gilles Hacheme, Michael Schmitt, Rahul Dodhia, Juan M. Lavista Ferres (Microsoft AI for Good); arXiv, Dec 2024, rev. Apr 2025
papers.rule: Post-hoc, label-free OOD detection for globally deployed EO models: generate surrogate in-distribution vs out-of-distribution labels from the frozen model's own feature space (no OOD examples needed), fit a light detector on those, and report against an upper bound with true OOD labels across covariate and semantic shifts.
papers.examines: Whether a shift in deployment imagery can be detected from internal activations of a frozen encoder; graded by OOD-detection AUROC against oracle-labelled shifts on EuroSAT, xBD and Fields of the World across 17 shift setups (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Near-upper-bound surrogate-labelling performance in 13 of 17 setups; matches top activation- and scoring-based post-hoc methods; code released (microsoft/geospatial-ood-detection).
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, adjacent to exp49 (SHRUG-FM U_E k-means/NCDD) and exp73 (kNN Sun 2022, Mahalanobis Lee 2018 lost 24/24 to the margin). TARDIS's surrogate-label estimator is a distinct construction (cluster ID features, treat far clusters as pseudo-OOD, train a binary detector) not yet raced against the margin; computable from the cached embedding bank. Headroom filter says it will likely lose as an error ranker, but it is the field's canonical label-free SHIFT detector, a different question from error ranking.

papers.title: Aligning Validation with Deployment in Spatial Prediction: Target-Weighted Cross-Validation
papers.authors_venue_year: Alexander Brenning, Thomas Suesse; arXiv, Mar 2026 (rev. May 2026)
papers.rule: When training/validation samples are preferentially or cluster sampled, weight validation cases so the validation task matches the deployment domain, using spatial task descriptors (environmental covariates, prediction distance); separate the generation of validation tasks from risk estimation (importance-weighted CV plus target-weighted CV).
papers.examines: Bias of cross-validated error estimates for spatial prediction models when the sample does not match the prediction domain; graded by bias of the estimated error against known truth in simulation and a Germany NO2 mapping case (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Weighted CV substantially reduces bias versus conventional CV in simulation; NO2 case study estimates more consistent with deployment conditions (no single headline number in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Partly covered by exp78 (design-based, stratified by confidence quintile, Neyman allocation, tile-cluster ratio estimator). Gap: exp78 weights by confidence strata, not by a deployment-domain descriptor (prediction distance / covariate dissimilarity to the training set). Successor to Olofsson 2014 / Stehman & Foody 2019 (known) on the sampling side.

papers.title: GEO-Bench-2: From Performance to Capability, Rethinking Evaluation in Geospatial AI
papers.authors_venue_year: Naomi Simumba, Nils Lehmann, Paolo Fraccaro, Hamed Alemohammad, Geeth De Mel, Salman Khan, Manil Maskey, Nicolas Longepe, Xiao Xiang Zhu, Hannah Kerner, Juan Bernabe-Moreno, Alexandre Lacoste; arXiv, Nov 2025 (rev. Feb 2026)
papers.rule: Rank GeoFMs only under a prescribed protocol: capped Bayesian HPO over a fixed space, task-type-defined adaptation heads, then repeat with five random seeds; report rankings per capability group (resolution, bands, temporality) rather than one global number, since no model is universally best.
papers.examines: Model ranking stability across 19 datasets and five task types; graded by per-capability-group ranking with seed repetition (abstract plus search-result summary of the protocol; five-seed detail is from a search summary, not the abstract).
papers.key_numbers: 19 datasets; 5 seeds; natural-image models (ConvNeXt-IN, DINOv3) lead on high-resolution tasks, EO models (TerraMind, Prithvi, Clay) on multispectral agriculture/disaster tasks.
papers.relation_to_record: Largely covered: exp79 runs 10 seeds x 24 tasks x 16 encoders; the tool uses Ai2's fixed probe recipe (no HPO). Gap: the record reports wins as counts over all 24 tasks; GEO-Bench-2's rule would also report the margin's lead per capability group (sensor, resolution, temporality) so a map user can see where it holds.

papers.title: Uncertainty and Generalizability in Foundation Models for Earth Observation
papers.authors_venue_year: Raul Ramos-Pollan, Freddie Kalaitzis, Karthick Panner Selvam; arXiv, Sep 2024
papers.rule: Under a fixed labelling budget, quantify a frozen FM's downstream performance AND its uncertainty by repeated resampling of the label set and of the area of interest; report the spread across AOIs, tasks and FMs, not a single score.
papers.examines: Spatial generalisability and label-sample variance of linear heads on 8 FMs over Sentinel-1/2 for ESA WorldCover class proportions across 11 AOIs; graded by correlation of chip-level predictions with truth and its variance over ~500,000 repeated linear fits (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 8 FMs, 11 AOIs, ~500k linear regressions; >0.9 correlation on chip-level tasks; performance and uncertainty vary greatly across AOIs, tasks and FMs.
papers.relation_to_record: Partly covered: exp79 gives seed floors; exp70/74 give per-task spread. Gap: no AOI-level (geographic block) resampling of the probe on record; the cached bank plus tile grids would allow it.

papers.title: Temporal Sensitivity Analysis of Tessera Embeddings
papers.authors_venue_year: Julia Guerrero-Viu, Alex Lopez-Cifuentes, Ignacio Perez-Villar, Fabio Pacifici; arXiv, 27 Aug 2026
papers.rule: Keep the encoder frozen and recompute embeddings over shrinking observation windows (year to day); report probe accuracy as a function of window length per class group, against from-scratch baselines, so that the temporal dependence of the representation is stated rather than assumed.
papers.examines: Inference sensitivity of a frozen annual-embedding encoder to the temporal window of its input, with a linear probe and a UNet head on LUCAS, DynamicEarthNet, PASTIS-R (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: PASTIS-R mIoU 58.3 (~46% above best from-scratch); year-to-month window cut costs 39% on PASTIS-R but 5% on DynamicEarthNet; single-day embeddings still 3.4x chance on LUCAS.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, but outside scope for single-date inputs (TESSERA parked per memory). Relevant rule for the tool's compare module: a dated-input sensitivity axis is a legitimate 'why errors are shared' explanation the tool does not compute.

papers.title: From Foundation Embeddings to Cropland Maps: Label Efficiency, Temporal Transferability and Independent Human Validation
papers.authors_venue_year: Mohammad Ammar Mughees, Giovanni Montefoschi, Zhongxin Chen, Maria Antonia Brovelli; arXiv, 15 Sep 2026
papers.rule: Validate a map produced from frozen embeddings with an independent, blind, two-interpreter consensus on a random point sample inside one contiguous held-out block, and compare agreement against the incumbent product on the same points with a paired test; test cross-year transfer of a classifier trained on one year.
papers.examines: Whether AlphaEarth annual embeddings plus a light classifier give a cropland map that holds across years and against independent interpreters; graded by held-out accuracy, blind-interpreter agreement and kappa (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 93.7% OA held-out; 90.8% balanced accuracy; 60k labelled pixels within 1.3 pp of 8.6M; blind 385-point block: 95.3% agreement (kappa 0.82) vs USDA CDL 91.7% (kappa 0.72, p=0.016); vs TerraMind 93.5% (p=0.14).
papers.relation_to_record: Adjacent to exp68 (LUCAS surveyor with design weights) and exp23 (WorldCover 2020 vs 2021 disagreement). Gap: no blind double-interpreter sample on the record; the record's paired reference comparisons use existing products, whose disagreement exp23 already showed exceeds model error.

papers.title: Characterizing AlphaEarth Embedding Geometry for Agentic Environmental Reasoning
papers.authors_venue_year: Mashrekur Rahman, Samuel J. Barrett, Christina Last; arXiv, 20 Apr 2026
papers.rule: Diagnose a geospatial embedding space label-free with participation ratio (effective dimensionality), local intrinsic dimension, and local-tangent-space rotation across locations; treat low local-global alignment as evidence that global vector arithmetic is invalid and that retrieval coherence must be predicted from local geometry.
papers.examines: Geometry of 12.1M AlphaEarth 64-d embeddings over CONUS 2017-2023; graded by intrinsic-dimension estimates, tangent-rotation angles, and R^2 of local geometry against retrieval coherence (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Participation ratio 13.3 of 64; local ID ~10; 84% of locations rotate >60 degrees; mean |cos| 0.17 vs 0.125 random; local geometry predicts retrieval coherence R^2=0.32.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. exp77 tested one scene direction; exp73 tested distance-based typicality. No per-region intrinsic-dimension or tangent-rotation diagnostic on record. Computable from the 792 GB cached bank per encoder; headroom filter applies if used as an error ranker, but as an embedding-quality diagnostic per tile it is a different deliverable.

papers.title: What on Earth is AlphaEarth? Hierarchical structure and functional interpretability for global land cover
papers.authors_venue_year: Ivan Felipe Benavides-Martinez et al. (Auroop R. Ganguly senior author); arXiv, 8 Mar 2026
papers.rule: Attribute each embedding dimension a functional role (specialist / generalist / high-generalist) via feature-importance patterns and progressive dimension ablation of the probe; report how many dimensions carry the task.
papers.examines: Which dimensions of a frozen embedding a land-cover probe actually uses; graded by probe accuracy under progressive ablation (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: 98% of baseline performance retained with only 2-12 of 64 dimensions.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap, low priority. The record never reports which embedding dimensions the probe leans on; could feed the explain module as a cue but does not pass filter 1 for a map user.

papers.title: Probing Geospatial SSL Representations with Environmental Signals
papers.authors_venue_year: Rohita Mocharla, Vishal M. Patel; arXiv, 6 Jul 2026
papers.rule: Evaluate a representation by probing it for physically co-varying environmental variables (ERA5 temperature, precipitation, radiation, pressure, soil moisture) co-located with the pretraining data; representation-level metrics separate models that tie on downstream benchmarks.
papers.examines: Whether frozen SSL encoders (DINO, MAE, MoCo on SSL4EO) encode physical covariates of the imaging process; graded by probe accuracy on ERA5 targets and its correlation with PANGAEA task performance (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: Three architectures under identical conditions; representation-level metrics distinguish models with similar downstream scores; ERA5 accessibility correlates with performance on environment-dependent PANGAEA tasks; ERA5 annotations for SSL4EO released.
papers.relation_to_record: Gap. Needs chip geolocation and dates (available for GEOID-Flood, not all Ai2 tasks). Label-free in the task sense (ERA5 is a free global covariate). Untested; unclear it passes filter 1.

papers.title: Scalable and Trustworthy Earth Observation Foundation Models
papers.authors_venue_year: Syed Usama Imtiaz, Mitra Nasr Azadani, Nasrin Alamdari; arXiv, 8 Jul 2026 (review / position)
papers.rule: Position: EO FMs must be assessed beyond benchmark accuracy on modality-aware transfer and physical plausibility of representations; inconsistent evaluation is named as the main obstacle to fair comparison and reliable deployment.
papers.examines: Review of RSFM design, adaptation and trustworthiness requirements; no experiment; grades nothing (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: None (review).
papers.relation_to_record: Position paper, weaker than 2605.12678 and 2608.16614 (both known). Citable in related_work as a 2026 trustworthiness position; imposes no estimator.

field_rules: Frozen-encoder robustness is reported as the drop from each model's own clean baseline, under compound product-defect chains as well as isolated corruptions, because chains fail beyond their strongest component (RSPDBench, 2609.23427).

Distribution shift at deployment is detected label-free from the frozen model's feature space using surrogate ID/OOD labels, and graded against an oracle-labelled shift upper bound across covariate and semantic shifts (TARDIS, 2412.13394).

A cross-validated error estimate is weighted so the validation task matches the deployment domain via spatial task descriptors such as prediction distance and covariate dissimilarity (Brenning & Suesse, 2603.29981).
Model rankings are only reported after capped HPO, fixed task-type heads and five seeds, and per capability group rather than as one global number (GEO-Bench-2, 2511.15658).
Downstream performance of a frozen FM is stated with its spread across areas of interest and repeated label resamples under a fixed budget (Ramos-Pollan et al., 2409.08744).

The temporal dependence of a frozen representation is measured by shrinking the observation window and reporting probe accuracy per class group against from-scratch baselines (Guerrero-Viu et al., 2608.27175).

A map from frozen embeddings is validated by a blind two-interpreter consensus on a random sample in a held-out block, with a paired test against the incumbent product on the same points (Mughees et al., 2609.17138).

Embedding spaces are diagnosed label-free by participation ratio, local intrinsic dimension and local-tangent rotation, and local geometry is required to predict retrieval coherence before global vector operations are trusted (Rahman et al., 2604.18715).
Representation quality is probed for physically co-varying environmental variables, which separates models that tie on task benchmarks (Mocharla & Patel, 2607.05207).

Calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability) is absent from all 152 GeoFM papers and drifts to overconfidence under shift; EO pretraining gives no more stability than ImageNet pretraining (Lehmann et al., 2608.16614, known).
gaps_in_our_tool: No degradation stress axis: the audit grades rankers on clean inputs only; the native-baseline rule of RSPDBench (2609.23427) and the shift-miscalibration finding of 2608.16614 (known) mean the margin's ranking quality under product defects (misregistration, radiometric gain, compound chains) is unmeasured; needs re-encoding, not cached embeddings.

No label-free SHIFT detector of the TARDIS kind (2412.13394): exp49/exp73 raced typicality and distance scores as error rankers, but the tool has no per-tile 'this imagery is off-distribution for the probe' flag built from surrogate ID/OOD labels in feature space; computable from the cached bank.

Error-rate estimation (exp78) stratifies by confidence quintile but does not weight the labelled sample toward the deployment domain by prediction distance or covariate dissimilarity as target-weighted CV requires (2603.29981); per-unit exports plus tile coordinates suffice to test the bias.
Seed variance is on record (exp79) but AOI-level resampling of the probe is not (2409.08744); the win counts do not say in which geographic blocks the margin's lead collapses.
Wins are reported over all 24 tasks; GEO-Bench-2 (2511.15658) would report them per capability group (sensor, resolution, temporality) so a map user sees where the margin's lead holds.

No embedding-geometry diagnostics per region (participation ratio, local intrinsic dimension, tangent rotation; 2604.18715) or per-dimension probe reliance (2603.16911); exp77 tested a single scene direction only.
No blind double-interpreter validation sample on record (2609.17138); paired references are existing products whose mutual disagreement (exp23) exceeds model error.
The compare module explains shared errors across dates but has no observation-window sensitivity axis (2608.27175); out of scope for single-date encoders but a stated omission.
