papers.title: Domino: Discovering Systematic Errors with Cross-Modal Embeddings
papers.authors_venue_year: Eyuboglu, Varma, Saab, Delbrouck, Lee-Messer, Dunnmon, Zou, Re; ICLR 2022 (oral)
papers.rule: A slice discovery method (SDM) must be graded quantitatively against planted or metadata-defined slices on two criteria at once: the slice underperforms AND it is coherent (united by a human-understandable concept); slices are found by an error-aware mixture model over (embedding, prediction, label), and each slice must be named in natural language and the name scored for exactness.
papers.examines: Post-hoc error clustering of a trained classifier's test set; grades SDMs by precision-at-k recovery of 1,235 known slices across natural images, medical images, time series, plus whether the generated text name matches the planted slice.
papers.key_numbers: 1,235 slice settings; Domino recovers 36% of slices (+12 pp over prior SDMs); exact slice name generated in 35% of settings (abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited (2203.14960 absent from the known list). Origin of the field's grading protocol for error regions. The reliability module's k-means over embeddings is an unsupervised cousin: Domino's mixture is fitted jointly on embedding + prediction + LABEL, so it is a grading-time tool, not a deployment tool. Gap: the tool has never graded its embedding clusters as slices (precision of recovering labelled error-dense regions) on the 24 tasks.

papers.title: The Spotlight: A General Method for Discovering Systematic Errors in Deep Learning Models
papers.authors_venue_year: d'Eon, d'Eon, Wright, Leyton-Brown; ACM FAccT 2022 (arXiv 2107.00758, 2021)
papers.rule: Systematic errors are found as CONTIGUOUS regions of the model's own final-hidden-layer space (a kernel-weighted 'spotlight' whose weight mass is lower-bounded and whose weighted loss is maximised), not as arbitrary subsets; the region, not the individual error, is the unit of report.
papers.examines: Contiguous high-loss regions in representation space of vision, NLP and recommender models; graded qualitatively by whether surfaced regions are semantically meaningful (abstract only).
papers.key_numbers: None in abstract; method applied across CV, NLP and recommender models.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Uses the model's own feature space (for the tool: the frozen encoder's embeddings the probe reads), which matches the tool's setting exactly. It needs per-unit loss (labels). Label-free variant possible: replace loss by 1-margin and ask whether the spotlight on low-margin windows is contiguous; not run in the record.

papers.title: Towards a More Rigorous Science of Blindspot Discovery in Image Classification Models (SpotCheck / PlaneSpot)
papers.authors_venue_year: Plumb, Johnson, Cabrera, Talwalkar; TMLR 2023 (arXiv 2207.04104)
papers.rule: Blindspot discovery methods must be evaluated on synthetic datasets with PLANTED blindspots (SpotCheck) so that discovery rate and false discoveries are measurable; and a method that appends the model's own confidence to a 2-D projection of the model's embedding (PlaneSpot) is competitive with cross-modal methods.
papers.examines: Recovery of known blindspots as a function of number of blindspots and the features defining them; validated on MS-COCO (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: No numbers in abstract; PlaneSpot 'competitive with and in many cases outperforms' prior BDMs on SpotCheck.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. PlaneSpot = embedding + confidence fed to an error-aware mixture, which is nearly the reliability module's k-means plus the margin, but with the label in the fit. The planted-blindspot protocol is a gap: the tool's Monte Carlo grading is for estimators (exp78), never for region discovery.

papers.title: Where Does My Model Underperform? A Human Evaluation of Slice Discovery Algorithms
papers.authors_venue_year: Johnson, Cabrera, Plumb, Talwalkar; AAAI HCOMP 2023 (best paper), arXiv 2306.08167
papers.rule: A discovered slice is only defensible if a human hypothesis formed from it is VERIFIED on held-out data (does the model actually underperform on all images matching the description); slice coherence does not imply hypothesis correctness, so a 'why' must be checked by a labelled test of the named group, not by visual coherence.
papers.examines: Controlled user study (N=15, 40 slices from Domino and PlaneSpot, object detection model); grades whether users' hypotheses about where the model underperforms are correct when checked against data.
papers.key_numbers: N=15, 40 slices (abstract). From search-result summaries, not the abstract: hypotheses correct 73% (Domino), 49% (PlaneSpot), 35% (random-error baseline); no significant association between slice coherence and hypothesis correctness.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Directly bears on the explain module: a cue with 'measured enrichment' is a coherence-style statement about flagged windows; the field's rule adds a second step, verify that the NAMED group (e.g. all windows with cue X) has elevated error on held-out labelled units, with a confidence interval. Gap unless the enrichment is computed on held-out units.

papers.title: Error Discovery by Clustering Influence Embeddings (InfEmbed)
papers.authors_venue_year: Wang, Adebayo, Tan, Garcia-Olano, Kokhlikyan; NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv 2312.04712)
papers.rule: Coherence should mean 'wrong for the same reason': cluster test examples by how they are influenced by the training data (influence embeddings, K-means), so a slice shares a training-data cause rather than an appearance.
papers.examines: Slice discovery on classification benchmarks; graded by recovery of known slices on two benchmarks plus debugging case studies (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: Outperforms state of the art on 2 benchmarks (abstract, no figures).
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. For a linear probe on frozen features, influence embeddings are cheap (closed-form for logistic regression) and would need the training features from the embedding bank, not only per-unit exports. Offers a different 'why': which training samples drove the error, compare/contrast with the tool's cue-enrichment 'why'. Untested.

papers.title: HiBug2: Efficient and Interpretable Error Slice Discovery for Comprehensive Model Debugging
papers.authors_venue_year: Chen, Zhao, Xu; ICLR 2025 (arXiv 2501.16751; successor of HiBug, NeurIPS 2023)
papers.rule: Group first by human-understandable attributes (LLM-proposed, VLM-annotated), then test each attribute combination for underperformance; report slices as attribute conjunctions and grade them by coherence and precision, and predict error slices beyond the validation set.
papers.examines: Classification, pose estimation, object detection; grades coherence and precision of slices and downstream repair (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: None in abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Attribute-first (name then test) is the opposite order to the tool's cluster-then-describe; the tool's label-free cues (boundary, band, texture) already are predefined attributes, so the explain module is closer to HiBug's flow than to Domino's. The missing piece is HiBug2's attribute-conjunction enumeration with a precision statistic per slice.

papers.title: Error Slice Discovery via Manifold Compactness (MCSD)
papers.authors_venue_year: Yu, Zou, Liu, Xu, He, Zhang, Cui; arXiv 2501.19032 (v2 Dec 2025)
papers.rule: Slice coherence must be measurable WITHOUT metadata: manifold compactness (a data-geometry statistic on the embedding manifold) is the coherence metric, and slice discovery should optimise risk and compactness jointly rather than describe clusters after the fact.
papers.examines: Post-hoc slice discovery on typical benchmarks; validates the compactness metric against metadata-defined slices, then uses it as the objective (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: None in abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Gives the reliability module a metadata-free coherence score for its k-means clusters, computable from cached embeddings alone; the record has no coherence statistic for any cluster. Risk term needs labels, but a margin-substituted version is label-free.

papers.title: Detecting Systematic Weaknesses in Vision Models along Predefined Human-Understandable Dimensions
papers.authors_venue_year: Gannamaneni, Rao, Mock, Akila, Wrobel; arXiv 2502.12360, 2025
papers.rule: Slices must align with operational-design-domain dimensions fixed in advance by domain experts; foundation models supply zero-shot metadata for those dimensions, a combinatorial search finds low-performance cells, and metadata noise from the foundation model is handled explicitly.
papers.examines: Recovery of planted systematic weaknesses on synthetic data and weaknesses of pretrained CV models on real data (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: None in abstract.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Predefined dimensions for EO would be land-cover class, season, sensor, terrain, cloud: the tool's task cards and compare module partly do this. Gap: no combinatorial search over cue conjunctions with a per-cell error statistic and a noise model for the cue itself.

papers.title: Automatic Discovery and Assessment of Interpretable Systematic Errors in Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors_venue_year: Singh, Singh, Kale, Gandhi; arXiv 2411.10845, 2024
papers.rule: For segmentation, a systematic error is a recurring (predicted class, target class) confusion on a coherent sub-group of objects; errors are retrieved on UNLABELLED data with multimodal foundation models, then grouped by conceptual linkage and error type and assessed for coherence.
papers.examines: UperNet ConvNeXt and Swin on Berkeley Deep Drive; qualitative and quantitative benchmark of discovered coherent systematic errors (abstract).
papers.key_numbers: None in abstract; two SOTA segmentation models, one dataset.
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Closest published attempt at label-free systematic-error discovery for segmentation; relies on a VLM as a pseudo-oracle, which does not exist for multispectral EO patches. The tool's compare module already reports shared-error 'why' across inferences but with no confusion-pair grouping; gap: no per-confusion-pair systematic-error report.

papers.title: GH-ESD: Grounded Hypothesis-Driven Error Slice Discovery for Instance-Level Vision Tasks
papers.authors_venue_year: Zhang, Wang, Guan, Kao, Zhao, Wu, He; ECCV 2026 (arXiv 2512.24592)
papers.rule: For detection and segmentation, slices are relational and spatially grounded, so the protocol is generate-and-verify: hypothesise a failure pattern (LLM prior plus grounded evidence), find instances matching it, then STATISTICALLY verify the slice against instance-level errors; grade with expert-defined grounded slices (GESD benchmark) by Precision@10.
papers.examines: Instance-level error slice discovery on detection and segmentation; new benchmark GESD with expert, spatially grounded slices.
papers.key_numbers: Precision@10 0.73 vs 0.63 for the best prior method on GESD detection (abstract/page summary).
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Sets the 2026 rule that a segmentation slice needs statistical verification, and supplies the Precision@10 grade. The tool's boundary finding (75% of errors on prediction boundaries) is a spatial slice with a verified statistic; the explain module's other cues lack a Precision@k-style grade.

papers.title: FALCON-Discover: Discovering Concentrated False-Confidence Regions for Calibration
papers.authors_venue_year: Cenacchi, Cao, Yang; arXiv 2607.18278, 2026
papers.rule: Measure false-confidence CONCENTRATION: the share of confident errors captured by a compact region of prediction space; rank predictions by DISCREPANCY between confidence, local support, neighbourhood agreement and perturbation stability, and report whether that recovers more dangerous-error mass than confidence alone, with cross-fitting over seeds.
papers.examines: Post-hoc, model-agnostic, on 7 binary tabular datasets with XGBoost/CatBoost, 4 seeds, 5-fold cross-fitting; grades recovery of high-confidence errors under a review budget.
papers.key_numbers: 7 datasets, 4 seeds, 5-fold; concentration 'recurrent but regime-dependent'; discrepancy ranking beats calibration and trust-score baselines in the strongest regimes (abstract/search summary; no figures in abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited (2607.17581 is known, this is a different id). Its ingredients (kNN support, neighbourhood contradiction, perturbation stability) each LOST to the margin in exp73 and the flood testbeds, so the ranking claim is likely already answered; the new piece is the concentration STATISTIC (fraction of confident errors inside the top-q compact region) which the record never computes and which is computable from per-unit exports plus cached embeddings.

papers.title: Active Slice Discovery in Large Language Models
papers.authors_venue_year: Zhang, Ijner, Wald, Creager; NeurIPS 2025 Reliable ML workshop (arXiv 2511.20713)
papers.rule: When labels are scarce, slice discovery is an active-learning problem: group likely-same-slice errors from embeddings, query an annotator only on whether selected samples share an error pattern, and grade by slice-recovery accuracy versus fraction of membership labels used.
papers.examines: Toxicity classification with LLMs; accuracy of recovered slices as a function of annotation budget, uncertainty-based querying vs baselines.
papers.key_numbers: Competitive slice recovery with 2-10% of slice-membership information (abstract).
papers.relation_to_record: Not cited. Matches the tool's 'small labelled sample may feed an estimator' scope: exp78 spends a review budget to estimate an error RATE; nobody has spent it to confirm or reject an error REGION. Gap: a budgeted region-verification loop over the reliability module's clusters.

field_rules: A reported error region must be both underperforming and coherent, and a method is graded by how many planted or metadata-defined slices it recovers, with the natural-language name scored for exactness (Domino, Eyuboglu et al. ICLR 2022).

Systematic errors are contiguous regions of the model's own representation space, so the region with a minimum mass and maximal weighted loss is the unit of report, not individual errors (Spotlight, d'Eon et al. FAccT 2022).

Discovery methods are validated on synthetic data with known blindspots so discovery and false-discovery rates are measurable, and appending the model's own confidence to a low-dimensional embedding is a strong baseline (SpotCheck/PlaneSpot, Plumb et al. TMLR 2023).
Coherence of a slice does not imply a correct hypothesis; a 'why' is defensible only when the named group is checked for elevated error on held-out data (Johnson et al. HCOMP 2023).
Coherence should mean 'wrong for the same reason', operationalised through training-data influence rather than appearance (InfEmbed, Wang et al. NeurIPS 2023).

Attribute-first discovery: propose human-understandable attributes, then enumerate attribute conjunctions and test each for underperformance, reporting per-slice precision (HiBug2, Chen et al. ICLR 2025).
Coherence needs a metadata-free geometric statistic (manifold compactness) so that risk and coherence can be optimised jointly (Yu et al. 2025).
Slices should be aligned to predefined operational-design-domain dimensions with an explicit noise model for foundation-model-derived metadata (Gannamaneni et al. 2025).
For segmentation the systematic error is a confusion pair on a coherent object sub-group, discoverable on unlabelled data via a foundation-model oracle (Singh et al. 2024).
Instance-level slices are spatial and relational and must be statistically verified after hypothesis generation, graded by Precision@10 on expert-defined slices (GH-ESD, Zhang et al. ECCV 2026).

False-confidence concentration (share of confident errors inside a compact region) is a reportable property, and discrepancy between confidence and structural signals is compared against confidence alone with cross-fitting (FALCON-Discover, Cenacchi et al. 2026).
With a label budget, slice discovery becomes active: query only whether selected samples share an error pattern and grade recovery against labels used (Zhang et al. NeurIPS 2025 workshop).
gaps_in_our_tool: No planted-slice or metadata-slice grading of the reliability module's k-means clusters: the field grades a discovery method by recovery precision of known error regions (Domino 2022; SpotCheck/PlaneSpot 2023); the tool grades rankers only (E-AURC, AUROC), never regions. Computable on the 24 tasks with labels as grader: fraction of labelled error mass inside the top-k clusters versus a random or margin-only partition.

No verification step for the explain module's 'why': Johnson et al. 2023 show coherent slices give wrong hypotheses about half the time; a cue enrichment measured on the same units that produced the cue is a coherence statistic, not a verified hypothesis. Rule: compute enrichment on held-out units (or separate seed exports) with a CI, and report the fraction of cues whose enrichment survives.

No statistical verification of segmentation slices in the GH-ESD sense (ECCV 2026): the boundary cue is verified (75% vs 21%), but other label-free cues have no Precision@k against labelled errors and no test that the named group as a whole underperforms.

No coherence statistic for clusters: manifold compactness (Yu et al. 2025) is metadata-free and computable from cached embeddings alone; the tool reports cluster membership without any coherence score, so a reader cannot tell a coherent failure region from a heterogeneous bin.

No false-confidence concentration statistic (FALCON-Discover 2026): the record shows confident errors exist but never reports what fraction of them sit inside a compact embedding region of size q; that number, per task and encoder, is computable from exp79 per-unit exports plus cached embeddings and would say whether confident errors can be found as regions at all.

No confidence-augmented embedding for region finding (PlaneSpot 2023 appends confidence to the embedding before fitting): the reliability module clusters embeddings alone and applies the margin afterwards; the field's baseline fits both jointly.

No attribute-conjunction enumeration (HiBug2 2025; Gannamaneni 2025): cues are reported one at a time with a single enrichment; the field enumerates conjunctions (e.g. boundary AND low-texture AND class X) with per-cell error statistics and a noise model for the cue itself.

No budgeted region-verification loop (Active Slice Discovery 2025): exp78 spends the review budget on a rate; the field also spends a few labels to confirm or reject each candidate region, reporting recovery versus labels used.

No training-data 'why' (InfEmbed 2023): for a linear probe on frozen features influence is closed-form, so 'which training samples drove this error cluster' is cheap from the embedding bank; the tool offers only input-side cues.

No per-confusion-pair systematic-error report for segmentation (Singh et al. 2024): the compare module says why errors are shared but does not group them by (predicted, reference) class pair on a coherent sub-group.

field_rule_audit.rule: Grade a confidence ranker by threshold-free risk-coverage areas (AURC/E-AURC, AUGRC) across many tasks, backbones and failure sources, never by one fixed-threshold metric.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Jaeger 2023; Traub 2024; Steinmetz 2026 (medRxiv 2026.05.04); Claros Olivares & Brockmeier 2025 (2511.11934)
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp70/exp74: E-AURC, AUROC and capture at 5/10/20% on 24 tasks x 16 encoders (exp/out/exp70_tasks.csv, exp74_summary.json); AUGRC computed in exp76 and agrees with AUROC ordering on 22 of 24 (docs/related_work.md section 7).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: Failure-detection scores are confounded with classifier accuracy; report excess or normalised metrics AND the correlation with accuracy explicitly.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Steinmetz 2026; Jaeger 2023
field_rule_audit.evidence: Excess AURC is the primary statistic. The correlation is never reported: computed from exp70/exp74 summaries while writing this audit, Spearman(test accuracy, margin AUROC) = 0.61 over 356 cells and Spearman(accuracy, E-AURC lead) = -0.46, i.e. the lead in E-AURC grows on worse maps because it is bounded by the error rate.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A reader cannot tell whether 'the margin ranks errors well on task T' is a fact about the ranking or about the probe being accurate; the two statistics move in opposite directions with accuracy and only one is shown.

field_rule_audit.rule: When many rankers are compared, control multiplicity (rank pipeline with family-wise control) and treat the winning family as a property of the representation, not the score.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Claros Olivares & Brockmeier 2025 (2511.11934)
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp73 and exp74 run one-sided sign tests per alternative and per encoder with no Holm/Bonferroni (exp/exp74_suite_encoders.py:171, exp73_alternatives_suite.py:312). Recorded p-values are 6e-8 (24/24) and 1.1e-4 (19/21); a Holm bar over 19 tests is 0.0026, so no verdict flips. The representation-statistic half (which encoder property predicts the ranker's margin) is not computed; headroom_by_encoder.json gives per-encoder headroom 0.55-0.69 without a predictor.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Low here: at the recorded p-values the correction changes nothing. The cost is a reviewer's objection, not a wrong claim.

field_rule_audit.rule: Misclassification and out-of-support inputs are graded jointly with a double-scoring risk-coverage metric (DS-AURC).
field_rule_audit.evidence: Every unit is in the label space by construction of Ai2's test splits; there is no OOD stratum, so an out-of-support window at deployment is either counted as an error against a wrong reference or not scored. No DS-AURC anywhere in exp/out.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A map built from imagery the probe has never seen (sensor artefact, unseen class) is ranked as if in-distribution; Lehmann 2026 (known) says the margin goes overconfident there. Cannot be graded inside the 24 tasks without an OOD stratum.

field_rule_audit.rule: In segmentation, the pixel-to-unit aggregation is a separately ablated component and ensemble pairwise disagreement is the baseline to beat.
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp76: five window aggregators on the seven segmentation tasks, gaps of order 0.001; exp73: 5-seed ensemble (vote disagreement, MI, bag margin) loses 22/24 to the margin (exp73_tasks.csv).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: Validate an uncertainty method by downstream use in controlled environments with injected ambiguity and shift; grade calibration alongside ranking.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Kahl et al. 2024 (ValUES)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Downstream uses are graded (review ordering at budgets, exp78 estimation). No injected ambiguity: exp23's reference disagreement is observational. ECE appears only in exp65 (0.159 on Bolivia fusion) and exp67; the margin's calibration on the 24 tasks is not graded.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Any deliverable that uses the margin as a probability rather than a rank (a label-free error estimate, a PPI predictor) inherits an ungraded bias.

field_rule_audit.rule: Linear-probe results are hyperparameter-sensitive; normalise probe inputs and check kNN/LP agreement before concluding about the representation.
field_rule_audit.evidence: The claim audited is 'this probe's own confidence ranks this probe's own errors'; a re-normalised probe is a different model with different errors, so the rule targets representation claims the record does not make. exp79 varies seeds; Ai2's recipe (probe_lrs recorded in the exp79 export) is fixed by design.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a for the ranking claim; applies only if the tool ever claims a property of the encoder rather than of a given probe.

field_rule_audit.rule: A ranking claim states its task-selection rule and shows stability under task subsets (benchmark lottery).
field_rule_audit.set_by: Dehghani et al. 2021 (2107.07002)
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp70 states the rule ('tasks we did not choose', Ai2's suite, one exclusion documented) and reports per task and per distinct source (14 sources, exp74_encoders.csv). The claims are per-task win counts, so any subset of a 24/24 result is still all wins; subset resampling adds nothing.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: Report geospatial rankings within capability groups (sensor, resolution, temporality) under a prescriptive protocol with seed repetition, not as one aggregate.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Simumba et al. GEO-Bench-2 (2511.15658); Ramos-Pollan et al. 2024 (2409.08744); Shang et al. 2026 (2606.29664)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Seeds: exp79 (10). Groups: only classification vs segmentation. No sensor/resolution/split-type table. From exp70_tasks.csv the median lead by sensor group is 0.113-0.131 (no sensor effect), while all 10 exp74 losses sit on cropharvest_Togo (n=306) or nandi_sentinel1 (accuracy 0.33); no AOI/tile-block spread of the lead is reported although the exports carry the tile grid.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A user of an S1 map or a small-region map cannot see that the thin cells (46 of 356 with lead < 0.03) are small-n / low-accuracy cells rather than a sensor property.

field_rule_audit.rule: Label-noise detectors and grades under imperfect references are validated against controlled, graded label perturbations.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Nogueira et al. 2026 (2603.00604)
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp23 measured reference instability (WorldCover 2020 vs 2021: 10.8% of errors vs 0.8% of correct windows changed class) and exp68 used a design-weighted survey; no controlled perturbation of the grading labels was run, and E-AURC's sensitivity to reference error is unmeasured.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The 24-task grades assume the reference is right; a random flip experiment would not model reference error, which exp23 shows is spatially structured, so the honest fix is a stated reviewer-error band on the estimate (see proposal 1), not a flip run.

field_rule_audit.rule: Reference data are imperfect: state the reference error rate and correct or bound accuracy and area estimates for it; bias grows for rare classes.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Foody 2024 (Geomatics 4(1)); CEOS LPV Land Cover protocol V1.1 (Nov 2025)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Olofsson 2014 and Stehman & Foody 2019 cited; references treated as fallible in exp23/exp68. `estimate` (oe_inferencex/estimate.py:360) treats the reviewer's 0/1 as exact; no sensitivity band; task cards do not state a reference error rate.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: exp78's honest interval is honest only for a perfect reviewer; with a 5% reviewer error on a map at 8% error the point estimate is biased by roughly the reviewer's error rate, larger than the interval half-width (0.029-0.031 at B=300).

field_rule_audit.rule: Robustness is the drop from each model's own clean baseline under physically grounded, compound product degradations.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Faruk et al. RSPDBench 2026 (2609.23427); Lehmann et al. 2026 (2608.16614, known)
field_rule_audit.evidence: All 24-task grades are on clean inputs; perturbations appear only as candidate signals (masking, tile phase, dihedral), never as an evaluation condition. related_work section 7 marks shift as 'never applied here'.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Whether the margin still ranks errors under misregistration or radiometric gain shift is unknown; needs new encoder passes, so out of tonight's scope.

field_rule_audit.rule: Splits must be region-disjoint and results reported per class, because foundation models collapse to frequent classes under regional shift.
field_rule_audit.evidence: Splits are Ai2's; exp70 records train-test gaps (so2sat 0.26, forestnet 0.23) that indicate some splits are shifted, but split type is not on the task cards (taskcard.py reads a splitter class only from olmoearth_run.yaml). No per-class error or boundary statistics; exp77 found scene-typicality confounded with class frequency.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The headline mixes region-disjoint and random splits, and the per-class collapse the field warns of is invisible in an overall error rate.

field_rule_audit.rule: A label-free accuracy estimate is graded by MAE between estimate and truth across many (model, shifted test set) pairs; it must be fitted on a labelled source split and applied to unlabelled targets; feature-distribution distances are not a substitute.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Garg et al. ICLR 2022 ATC (2201.04234); Guillory et al. ICCV 2021 DoC (2107.03315)
field_rule_audit.evidence: The tool's position is that 'how wrong' needs a reference (Usage). No ATC/DoC is computed. The record does contain an implicit label-free estimate: exp78's D2c allocation uses mean(1 - p1) per stratum as the stratum error rate; its calibration as a point estimate is never graded. The exports (margin, p1, dec, err, y) and 356 cells suffice to grade one.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The tool cannot say anything about a map's error rate before a single label is spent, although the field has estimators with declared failure modes that run on what the tool already exports.

field_rule_audit.rule: With a family of models, unlabelled pairwise agreement lies on the accuracy line; for probed foundation models the family must differ by random head initialisation.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Baek et al. NeurIPS 2022 (2206.13089); Saxena et al. 2024 (2404.01542)
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp73 used seed disagreement only as an instance ranker (lost 22/24). The 10-seed x 16-encoder family exists (exp79) but only seed-0 per-unit decisions are exported (exp79_seed_floors.py:108-113), so agreement cannot be computed tonight.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The cheapest dataset-level error estimate the field has for exactly this asset (random-init linear heads) is untested; needs a per-seed decision export job.

field_rule_audit.rule: Confidence-based estimators underestimate error under pseudo-label/prevalence shift; use an optimal-transport cost to the source marginal and grade under label-shift cases separately.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Lu et al. NeurIPS 2023 COT (2305.15640); Fluehmann et al. 2025 (2507.22776)
field_rule_audit.evidence: No label-free estimator exists yet, so nothing to correct. Prevalence shift between train and test is measurable per task once the training label marginal is read from the cached bank (one cluster job); between tile-block halves of a test split it is measurable from the exports' y.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Becomes 'violates' the moment proposal 4 ships without its prevalence-shift grade; EO maps shift prevalence by region and date (flood extent, crop mix).

field_rule_audit.rule: Dataset-level scores are compared by correlation with true accuracy; survivors are logit-matrix statistics with an overconfidence correction (nuclear norm, MaNo) or the one-step head-gradient norm (GdScore), with class imbalance declared as a failure mode.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Deng et al. ICML 2023 (2302.01094); Xie et al. NeurIPS 2024 (2405.18979); Xie et al. TMLR 2025 (2401.08909)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Not computed; needs full probability vectors, which the exports lack (margin and p1 only); one CPU/GPU job per encoder on the cached bank.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Only matters if ATC/DoC (computable tonight) fail on the imbalanced segmentation tasks; ordered behind them.

field_rule_audit.rule: Estimate the confusion matrix, not accuracy, when users need per-class metrics; report behaviour separately under covariate and prevalence shift.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Fluehmann et al. 2025 (2507.22776)
field_rule_audit.evidence: `estimate` returns one error rate with an interval (estimate.py:360-431). The per-unit exports carry y and dec, so a labelled confusion matrix per task is computable without new labels; a label-free one is not attempted.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A map user gets 'the map is 8% wrong' and not 'water is missed 20% of the time', which is the number a flood-response user acts on.

field_rule_audit.rule: Per-image segmentation quality without a label is estimated by reverse classification against a small reference set and reported as a conformal interval.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Cosarinsky et al. IEEE TMI 2025 (2503.04522)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Needs an in-context segmenter over retrieved references, not the frozen probe (filter 2: no new head as deliverable).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: Instance-level consistency under semantics-preserving perturbation is graded as a correctness likelihood by calibration error, and segmentation error is decomposed into identity-flip vs omission before any label-free flag is judged.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Nam et al. WACV 2026 SICL (2512.07390); Achara et al. 2026 (2604.13326)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Consistency signals (tile phase, dihedral, masking, shift-TTA exp53) were graded as rankers and lost; never as calibration. The record's error axis is boundary vs interior; identity flip vs omission is absent although y and dec on the six multi-class segmentation tasks allow it.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The explain module cannot say whether a flagged region is the right object with the wrong class or a missed object, which decides the user's fix (relabel vs redraw).

field_rule_audit.rule: Never estimate a population quantity from predictions alone; use a probability sample of reference labels and treat the model output as an auxiliary variable for variance reduction only.
field_rule_audit.set_by: CEOS LPV protocol 2025; Lu, Kluger, Bates, Wang 2024/2025 (2407.13659)
field_rule_audit.evidence: `sample`/`estimate` are design-based (Wilson/Korn-Graubard, stratified, ratio estimator); exp78 graded coverage by Monte Carlo (P1 holds 7/7 at 0.93); a guard rejects estimating from the review set (2-6x bias).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: Use the predictions on unlabelled units through a debiased difference/PPI estimator with a data-tuned coefficient so the interval is never wider than the labelled-only one; tune per stratum when accuracy varies across strata.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Angelopoulos, Duchi, Zrnic PPI++ (2311.01453); Fisch et al. NeurIPS 2024 StratPPI (2406.04291)
field_rule_audit.evidence: docs/plan/map_error_estimation.md lists arm E3d (difference estimator, g = 1 - p1, cross-fitted by tile) but exp78's run_designs has no such arm and exp78_summary.json has only D1/E1, D2p/E1, D2c/E1, D2star/E1, D1+E3ps, D4/E2_naive, D4/E1_cluster. The digest's sentence 'a difference estimator with confidence as predictor was an arm' is therefore not backed by the record.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The predictions on the unlabelled 99.9% of units contribute nothing to the estimate; and an unrun arm is being described as run, which the audit-before-record rule forbids.

field_rule_audit.rule: If the model's uncertainty chooses which units get labelled, weight by inclusion probabilities and mix with uniform sampling so a badly ranked case is never worse than random.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Zrnic & Candes ICML 2024 (2403.03208); Li, Zrnic, Candes NeurIPS 2025 (2511.08991)
field_rule_audit.evidence: D2c is a one-shot Neyman allocation from the model's confidence with a per-stratum floor (estimate.neyman_allocation, MIN_PER_STRATUM), i.e. a bounded version of confidence-driven inclusion; exp78 shows D2c within 0.0007 of the oracle allocation D2star on MADOS and Sen1Floods11, so the allocation has no headroom left for an active rule to claim.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Low: the record's own ceiling arm says allocation is saturated; the guard the field adds is already implicit in the stratum floor.

field_rule_audit.rule: For clustered or stratified labelled samples, PPI intervals must come from a design-aware bootstrap, not i.i.d. formulas.
field_rule_audit.evidence: No PPI arm exists; the classical tile-cluster ratio estimator uses ultimate-cluster variance (estimate.cluster_interval). Becomes binding for proposal 5 on the tile design.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a until a PPI arm runs on tile draws; then coverage failure of the kind exp78 recorded for D4/E2_naive (0.51-0.82).

field_rule_audit.rule: Strata for accuracy estimation are best formed by clustering a predicted per-unit performance score rather than fixed confidence bins; model-assisted estimators beat labelled-only ones.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Fogliato, Patil, Monfort, Perona ECCV 2024
field_rule_audit.evidence: Strata are margin quintiles (estimate.confidence_strata). The oracle arm D2star bounds what any stratification can buy: D2c half-width 0.01858 vs D2star 0.01797 on MADOS, 0.02497 vs 0.02494 on Sen1Floods11 (exp78_summary.json). Fogliato's 10x is against SRS on low-error tasks; the record's model-free ceiling from capture@20% is 1.66x (plan P4).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: None measurable: the strata cannot beat the oracle allocation they already sit next to; the model-assisted gain must come from the estimator (PPI), which is the violated rule above.

field_rule_audit.rule: A map user is owed user's accuracy, producer's accuracy and error-adjusted area per class with standard errors; an allocation chosen for one target degrades the others, most for a rare class.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Stehman & Wagner RSE 2023; CEOS LPV protocol 2025 (75-150 units per map-class stratum)
field_rule_audit.evidence: `estimate` reports overall error only; no UA/PA/area anywhere in oe_inferencex (grep for producer/user's accuracy finds only the Dawid-Skene confusion in evidence.py). The exports carry y, dec and margin, so all three are computable from exp78's Monte Carlo without new labels.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The tool's 'how wrong is the map' does not meet the field's definition of an accuracy assessment, and Neyman-on-confidence may be starving the rare class the user cares about (water in a flood map).

field_rule_audit.rule: Sample size is planned backwards from a target coefficient of variation using the map's PA/UA-driven relative efficiency.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Adebayo et al. IJAEOG 2026; RSE 2025 companion
field_rule_audit.evidence: The tool grades a given budget; exp78 has half-widths at B in {100, 300, 1000} per task, the ingredients of a planner, but no `sample --target-cv` exists.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A user must guess B; the field's answer ('n for 10% CV given this map') is one function of numbers the record already holds.

field_rule_audit.rule: Beyond an estimate with an interval, a deployable guarantee is a threshold chosen so a monotone risk (missed-error rate) is at most alpha on new data.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, Schuster ICLR 2024 CRC (2208.02814); Learn then Test AoAS 2025 (2110.01052)
field_rule_audit.evidence: The tool orders review by margin and reports capture at fixed budgets (exp70); no threshold with a risk bound is produced. Li et al. 2026 conformal SAR flood is cited (known) but not implemented.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A user who reviews the top 10% learns afterwards what they caught; they cannot ask for 'a review set that leaves at most alpha missed errors' in advance.

field_rule_audit.rule: Label-efficient risk estimation can be sequential: acquire the next label where it most reduces variance, with prediction-based control variates.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Ashouritaklimi et al. 2026 PPAT (2607.08347); Ye, Lyu, Tao 2026 (2604.12497)
field_rule_audit.evidence: One-shot design only. exp78 P4 bounds any saving at 1.8x vs SRS (max recorded 2.5x for the oracle arm), and D2c sits at the oracle allocation, so a sequential design can only recover the pilot-estimate gap, which D2c does not have.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Small by the record's own bound; a reviewer-in-the-loop design costs more than it returns here.

field_rule_audit.rule: A confidence or algorithm-variance layer is not an accuracy assessment; documentation must say which outputs are assessments in the protocol's sense.
field_rule_audit.set_by: CEOS LPV protocol 2025, executive summary and chapter 3
field_rule_audit.evidence: Usage says `estimate` needs a labelled sample and the guard rejects review-set estimation; the docs do not say in the protocol's words that `assess`'s ranking and the explain cues are review-ordering aids and only `sample`/`estimate` are an accuracy assessment.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A reader of the task cards may take capture-at-budget for an accuracy statement.

field_rule_audit.rule: Distribution shift at deployment is detected label-free from the frozen model's feature space with surrogate ID/OOD labels and graded against an oracle-labelled shift.
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp49 (SHRUG-FM U_E) and exp73 (kNN, Mahalanobis, 24/24 losses) graded typicality as error rankers, a different question; no per-scene 'off-distribution for this probe' flag exists, and the 24 tasks have no oracle-labelled shift stratum (only the Bolivia flood split).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The one condition the record knows the margin fails in (shift, per Lehmann 2026) is the one the tool cannot flag.

field_rule_audit.rule: Weight a cross-validated error estimate so the validation task matches the deployment domain via spatial task descriptors.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Brenning & Suesse 2026 (2603.29981)
field_rule_audit.evidence: `estimate`'s estimand is the error rate of the map at hand, and the sample is drawn from that map (a census of its units), so validation-to-deployment reweighting does not arise; it would apply only to transferring a 24-task grade to a new region, which the tool does not claim.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: The temporal dependence of a frozen representation is measured by shrinking the observation window.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Guerrero-Viu et al. 2026 (2608.27175)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Single-date encoders and single-date chips throughout the suite (TESSERA parked per memory).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a

field_rule_audit.rule: A map from frozen embeddings is validated by a blind two-interpreter consensus on a random sample in a held-out block, with a paired test against the incumbent product.
field_rule_audit.evidence: exp26 hand-check kit and exp68 LUCAS surveyor exist; no blind double interpretation, so the reviewer error rate that rule 11 needs is unmeasured.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: The reviewer-error band on the estimate has no measured input; a data-collection task, not a methodology change.

field_rule_audit.rule: Embedding spaces are diagnosed label-free by participation ratio, local intrinsic dimension and tangent rotation; representations are probed for co-varying environmental variables; probe reliance per dimension is reported.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Rahman et al. 2026 (2604.18715); Mocharla & Patel 2026 (2607.05207); Benavides-Martinez et al. 2026 (2603.16911)
field_rule_audit.evidence: Not computed. exp73 and exp77 and claim no-encoder-internal-signal-beats-confidence: feature-space statistics carried no error information as rankers; none of the three maps to a statement a map user acts on.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: None for a map user; fails filter 1.

field_rule_audit.rule: Calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability) must be reported and drifts to overconfidence under shift.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Lehmann et al. 2026 (2608.16614, known)
field_rule_audit.evidence: ECE in exp65/exp67 only; not graded for the margin on the 24 tasks; exp70's train-test gaps (so2sat 0.26, forestnet 0.23) mark the cells where overconfidence is expected.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: A label-free estimate built on p1 is biased exactly on those cells; the ranking deliverable is unaffected because it uses ranks.

field_rule_audit.rule: A reported error region must be both underperforming and coherent; discovery methods are graded by recovery of planted or metadata slices on synthetic data with known blindspots; coherence needs a metadata-free statistic.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Eyuboglu et al. ICLR 2022 Domino; d'Eon et al. FAccT 2022 Spotlight; Plumb et al. TMLR 2023 SpotCheck; Yu et al. 2025 MCSD
field_rule_audit.evidence: The tool ships no region-discovery deliverable: oe_inferencex/reliability.kmeans has no callers in the package (grep), it is a leftover of exp49. The record's region statements are the boundary finding (75% vs 21%) and the tile design effect (1.2-9.8), both verified spatial statistics.
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: n/a; would become binding if a cluster-based region report were ever shipped.

field_rule_audit.rule: Coherence of a slice does not imply a correct hypothesis; a 'why' is defensible only when the named group is checked for elevated error on held-out data; instance slices must be statistically verified (Precision@k).
field_rule_audit.set_by: Johnson, Cabrera, Plumb, Talwalkar HCOMP 2023 (2306.08167); Zhang et al. ECCV 2026 GH-ESD (2512.24592)
field_rule_audit.evidence: explain.CUES quotes enrichments measured with tile-clustered bootstrap CIs on one testbed (boundary 0.750 vs 0.214, Bolivia; explain.py:62-72) and applies them to any map; the record notes 'narrower scope on many-class tasks' but no per-task recomputation on the 24 tasks is on file, although boundary and low_confidence are computable from the exports (dec, grid, margin, err).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: On a PASTIS map the explain module quotes a Bolivia flood number; the field's finding is that about half of coherent-looking hypotheses are wrong when checked, so the quoted 'why' is a hypothesis presented as a measurement.

field_rule_audit.rule: Attribute-first discovery: predefined human-understandable attributes, conjunctions enumerated and tested per cell, with a noise model for the attribute itself.
field_rule_audit.set_by: Chen, Zhao, Xu ICLR 2025 HiBug2 (2501.16751); Gannamaneni et al. 2025 (2502.12360)
field_rule_audit.evidence: The cue library is attribute-first and explain.cooccurrence reports pairwise co-occurrence; no per-conjunction error statistic and no noise model for a cue (e.g. boundary computed from the map's own decisions).
field_rule_audit.consequence_if_violated: Cues that co-occur (boundary and low_confidence overlap by construction) are counted as two reasons for one error.

field_rule_audit.rule: For segmentation the systematic error is a (predicted, reference) confusion pair on a coherent object sub-group.
field_rule_audit.evidence: compare reports why errors are shared across two inferences; no confusion-pair grouping in explain or compare; y and dec in the exports allow the labelled version on the six multi-class segmentation tasks.

proposals.name: Per-class accuracy assessment from the same labelled sample: user's accuracy, producer's accuracy and error-adjusted area with standard errors, a class-aware allocation, and a sample-size planner
field_rules_followed: CEOS LPV protocol 2025: UA/PA/area from the reference sample, 75-150 units per map-class stratum
Stehman & Wagner 2023: allocation trade-off across UA, PA and area, worst for rare classes
Fluehmann et al. 2025: estimate the confusion matrix, not accuracy
Adebayo et al. 2026: plan n backwards from a target CV
Foody 2024: state a reviewer-error band
Shang et al. 2026: report per class
proposals.what_changes: `estimate` returns, beside the overall error rate, the labelled confusion matrix of the sample and design-based UA_c, PA_c and error-adjusted area A_c per map class with SEs (Olofsson 2014 estimators on the stratified sample, ratio form on tile draws), plus a reviewer-error band (estimate recomputed under a stated reviewer error rate e in {0, 0.02, 0.05}). `sample` gains design D3: strata = predicted class x margin half, with the CEOS floor per map-class stratum, and `sample --target-cv 0.10` returns the B that reaches it from the class rates. exp78's Monte Carlo (R=2000) is extended to grade UA/PA/area coverage per class on every (task, encoder) cell of the exp79 export. Docs state, in the protocol's words, that only `sample`/`estimate` are an accuracy assessment and `assess` is a review-ordering aid.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: 'Water is missed 19% of the time and 12% of mapped water is not water, so the flooded area is 8.1 +/- 0.9 km2 not 9.4' instead of 'the map is 8% wrong'. That is the number a flood or crop user acts on and the number the field's standard says a producer owes.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes: per-class omission/commission and corrected area are unknowable from the map today and are what CEOS/Olofsson define as the assessment.
proposals.filter_2_audit_scope: Passes: no training, no head; labels come from the same small review sample the tool already asks for; the map's own decisions define the strata.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Not a ranker; the margin's ranking is kept as the stratifier. The headroom bound that applies is exp78's: D2c is within 0.0007 half-width of the oracle allocation, so the gain is in what is reported, not in the interval width.
proposals.already_in_record: exp78 (overall error rate, 7 segmentation tasks, D1/D2p/D2c/D2star/E3ps/D4 arms) and exp68 (LUCAS with design weights, overall). Nothing per class; grep finds no UA/PA in the package. Not a repeat: same sample, new estimands and a class-aware design.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Estimands: UA_c, PA_c, A_c per class c, overall theta, per (task, encoder), truth from y and dec in the export. Arms: D1/E1 (SRS), D2c/E1 (record), D3 (class x margin-half strata, CEOS floor). B = 300 headline, {100, 300, 1000} reported, R = 2000. P1 (honesty): for every class with at least 30 sampled units the UA_c and PA_c intervals cover at 0.93 or better on every cell (exp78 P1 bar 0.93; exp79 P5's Monte Carlo tolerance max(0.01, 3 SE)). P2 (Stehman & Wagner): under D2c at B = 300 the rarest class's UA half-width exceeds twice the overall half-width (exp78 overall half-widths 0.018-0.053) on all 7 segmentation tasks. P3 (allocation trade-off): D3 cuts the rarest-class UA half-width by at least 20% against D2c while widening the overall half-width by at most 10%; failing P3 means the class-aware design costs the overall estimate more than it buys. P4 (Olofsson): error-adjusted area differs from pixel-count area by more than one SE for at least one class on at least 5 of 7 segmentation tasks. P5 (planner): the B predicted for a 10% CV on theta from exp78's half-widths at {100, 300, 1000} is within 15% of the Monte Carlo B. P6 (reviewer error, Foody): at reviewer error e = 0.05 the overall estimate's bias exceeds the B = 300 half-width on both tasks with theta < 0.10 (mados, sen1floods11, half-widths 0.029-0.031).
proposals.how_it_could_fail: On the 19-class PASTIS tasks most classes get under 30 units at B = 300, so per-class intervals are Wilson-at-tiny-n and P1 is untestable there; that is itself the CEOS answer (budget scales with classes) and must be reported, not hidden. Classification tasks have no area meaning (area only for segmentation). Ai2's test splits are not a map's class mix, so the Monte Carlo grades the estimator, not a deployment.

proposals.name: A verification rule for `explain`: every cue's enrichment is recomputed per task on held-out units with a clustered CI, the library value is quoted only where it survives, and multi-class segmentation errors are reported by confusion pair and by flip-vs-omission
field_rules_followed: Johnson et al. HCOMP 2023: a 'why' is defensible only when the named group is verified on held-out data
Zhang et al. GH-ESD ECCV 2026: statistical verification of instance slices, Precision@k
Singh et al. 2024: segmentation systematic error = confusion pair
Achara et al. 2026: identity-flip vs omission decomposition
HiBug2 2025: per-conjunction cell statistics
proposals.what_changes: A grading stage `explain --verify` runs on every (task, encoder) export: for each cue computable label-free from the export (boundary from dec and the tile grid; low_confidence from margin; their conjunction), the share among errors, share among correct, enrichment ratio and Precision@k at the record's budgets (5, 10, 20%) with explain.cue_enrichment's tile-clustered bootstrap CI. explain.CUES gains a per-task table; at deployment the module quotes the verified value for the task family at hand and prints 'library value from Bolivia, unverified on this task type' otherwise. For multi-class segmentation, `explain` adds the top confusion pairs (labelled grade) and, label-free, the flip-risk cue (entropy over foreground classes, Achara) and the flip-vs-omission split against a background class where one exists.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: The 'why' beside a flagged window becomes a number measured on maps like theirs with an interval, or an honest 'unverified'; and on a crop map they learn 'most errors are maize-vs-sorghum on field edges', which decides relabel vs redraw.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes: which cue explanations are trustworthy for their task type, and the dominant confusion, are unknowable today.
proposals.filter_2_audit_scope: Passes: labels grade only; cues remain label-free; no new head.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Not a ranker. The verification may shrink what the explain module claims; that is the point.
proposals.already_in_record: exp37 (cue enrichment, Bolivia) and claims cue-enrichment-table, errors-sit-on-boundaries (75% vs 21%), boundary-first-review-order ('narrower scope on many-class tasks'). Not a repeat: those are one testbed; nothing per task on the 24-task suite, no confusion-pair or flip/omission report anywhere.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Estimand per (task, encoder, cue): share of errors carrying the cue (s_e), share of correct windows (s_c), ratio s_e/s_c, tile-clustered 95% CI (n_boot = 2000, explain.cue_enrichment). P1: boundary ratio >= 2 on at least 6 of 7 OlmoEarth Base segmentation tasks (Bolivia 0.750/0.214 = 3.5; the record's many-class caveat predicts the PASTIS 19-class tasks as the likely miss). P2: the library values 0.750 and 0.214 fall outside the per-task CI on at least 4 of 7 tasks, establishing that quoting Bolivia on another task is wrong by the record's own CI. P3: across the 16 encoders at least 75% of (encoder, segmentation task) cells keep ratio >= 2 (exp74's 75% bar). P4 (conjunction): boundary AND low_confidence has Precision@5% at least 0.05 above boundary alone on at least 5 of 7 tasks, otherwise the two cues are one reason and the module must say so. P5 (confusion pairs): on the six multi-class segmentation tasks the top three (predicted, reference) pairs hold at least 50% of errors on at least 4 of 6. P6 (flip vs omission): the label-free flip-risk cue's enrichment ratio >= 1.5 for identity flips on at least 3 of the tasks that have a background class; if it fails, the cue is not added.
proposals.how_it_could_fail: Boundary computed from the map's own decisions is noisier on 19-class maps (every class change is a boundary), so the ratio can collapse without the mechanism changing; P1's expected miss must be reported by class count, not averaged away. Precision@k on classification tasks with 200-306 units (awf, Togo) has CIs too wide to verify anything; those cells are reported as unverifiable, not as failures.

proposals.name: Where the lead holds: a capability-group, split-type and spatial-block re-tabulation of the headline, with the accuracy confound and multiplicity reported
field_rules_followed: Steinmetz 2026 / Jaeger 2023: report the correlation of failure-detection score with accuracy
GEO-Bench-2 (Simumba 2025): report per capability group
Ramos-Pollan 2024: spread across areas of interest
Shang 2026: stratify by split type and class frequency
Claros Olivares 2025: family-wise control over the raced alternatives
CEOS 2025: say which outputs are an accuracy assessment
proposals.what_changes: A committed script re-tabulates exp70/exp74/exp79 by sensor group (S1, S2, Landsat, multi), task family, class count, unit count and split type (from Ai2's task metadata, added to the task cards), and reports Spearman(accuracy, margin AUROC) and Spearman(accuracy, E-AURC lead) over all cells with a bootstrap CI; Holm over the 16 encoder sign tests and the exp73 alternatives; and on the 7 segmentation tasks the per-tile-block E-AURC lead via stats.block_bootstrap_indices, reported as a 10th-percentile-across-blocks. The Findings page states the headline with these strata beside it.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: Whether the margin's lead applies to their sensor, region size and map type, and that the thin cells are small-n or low-accuracy cells rather than a sensor property; and the confound: the ranking statistic (AUROC) rises with probe accuracy, so a bad probe ranks its errors worse.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes: today the user sees 24/24 and cannot locate their own case in it.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Not a ranker; it qualifies the existing claim.
proposals.already_in_record: exp70/74 report per task and per distinct source; exp79 adds seeds; docs/related_work section 7 says the spatial support of the 24 tasks is not characterised. Not a repeat: no group table, no confound statistic, no block spread, no Holm. Computed while writing this audit from committed summaries: 356 cells, Spearman(accuracy, AUROC) = 0.61, Spearman(accuracy, lead) = -0.46; all 10 exp74 losses on cropharvest_Togo (n = 306) or nandi_sentinel1 (accuracy 0.33); sensor-group median leads 0.113-0.131.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Because the seed-0 statistics were seen while auditing, the predictions are stated on the exp79 reseeded cells. P1 (confound): Spearman(accuracy, margin AUROC) >= 0.5 under every one of the 10 seeds (seed-0 value 0.61), and the sign of Spearman(accuracy, E-AURC lead) is negative under every seed. P2 (thin cells belong to small or bad cells, not sensors): every (encoder, task) loss under any seed is on a task with n <= 306 or accuracy <= 0.40 (the seed-0 pattern); the median lead by sensor group differs by at most 0.03 between groups (seed-0 range 0.113-0.131). P3 (multiplicity): Holm over the 19 sign tests (16 encoders + ensemble, kNN, Mahalanobis) changes no verdict (smallest recorded p 1.1e-4 for 19/21 against a Holm bar of 0.0026). P4 (block spread): on at least 6 of 7 segmentation tasks the 10th percentile across tile blocks of the margin's E-AURC lead over the best control is above 0; the task that fails is named with its blocks. P5 (split type): on region-disjoint tasks the median lead is within 0.03 of random-split tasks; if it is not, the headline is re-stated per split type.
proposals.how_it_could_fail: Split type for the 24 tasks may not be fully documented upstream (Ai2 inherits GEO-Bench and CropHarvest splits), leaving P5 partly unclassifiable; the block spread depends on block size, which must be fixed to exp78's tile before looking. The confound correlation is descriptive; the record's remedy stays excess AURC, and P1 only forces the number onto the page.

proposals.name: A label-free error-rate estimate with a declared failure mode: ATC and DoC on the margin, graded by MAE across all cells and by prevalence shift between tile-block halves, then used as the pilot for `sample`
field_rules_followed: Garg et al. 2022 ATC: fit one threshold on a labelled source, apply to unlabelled target, grade by MAE across many (model, set) pairs
Guillory et al. 2021 DoC
Lu et al. 2023 / Fluehmann et al. 2025: grade separately under prevalence shift; confidence-based estimators underestimate error there
Lehmann 2026 (known): overconfidence under shift
CEOS 2025: a confidence layer is not an accuracy assessment (so the output is labelled a pilot, not an assessment)
proposals.what_changes: `estimate --label-free` returns a point estimate of the map's error rate from margin/p1 alone, with the source threshold fitted on the probe's labelled validation split (the tool already holds the probe) and a printed failure mode ('assumes the class mix of this map matches the training split; under prevalence shift this underestimates'). `sample` uses the ATC-calibrated stratum rates in place of raw mean(1 - p1) for Neyman allocation (D2c'). Grading: on every (task, encoder) export, split by tile blocks (segmentation) or at random (classification) into source and target halves; ATC, DoC and the naive mean(1 - p1) estimate the target error; MAE across 356 cells; signed error against the prevalence shift |Delta class marginal| between halves computed from y.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: Before spending one label: 'this map is roughly 9% wrong, unless its class mix differs from training, in which case more'. Today the tool says nothing until 300 labels arrive.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes: a pre-label estimate with a stated failure mode is new information; labelling it a pilot keeps it honest.
proposals.filter_2_audit_scope: Passes: label-free at deployment; the source threshold uses the probe's own validation labels, which exist for any probed model.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Not a ranker. The allocation headroom is already gone (D2c within 0.0007 of D2star in exp78), so D2c' is predicted to gain nothing; the value is the estimate itself.
proposals.already_in_record: exp78's D2c uses mean(1 - p1) per stratum as an implicit label-free stratum rate for allocation only; its calibration as an estimate is ungraded. exp70 holds train-test gaps per task (so2sat 0.26, forestnet 0.23) that predict where p1 overconfidence breaks it. Not a repeat: no label-free point estimate has been produced or graded.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Estimand: target-half error rate per cell. Arms: naive mean(1 - p1), ATC on margin, DoC on p1 with a linear map fitted across the classification tasks' source halves. P1: ATC's MAE is at most the exp78 B = 300 SRS half-width (0.029-0.031) on the two low-error segmentation tasks (mados, sen1floods11) and on m_eurosat and m_brick_kiln for OlmoEarth Base. P2 (overconfidence): the naive estimate's ratio to truth is below 0.7 on every task whose exp70 train-test gap exceeds 0.20 (so2sat, forestnet, and the nandi/cropharvest S1 tasks where recorded), and ATC halves that shortfall. P3 (Lu 2023): across cells the signed ATC error correlates with the prevalence shift between halves, Spearman >= 0.3, and the sign is underestimation when the target's majority class shrinks. P4 (honesty): ATC's MAE exceeds the labelled B = 300 half-width on at least one third of all cells, so the output is documented as a pilot for allocation and a sanity check, never as the accuracy assessment. P5 (allocation): D2c' half-width is within 0.002 of D2star on every segmentation task (D2c already is within 0.0007 on mados and sen1floods11), i.e. no allocation gain is claimed.
proposals.how_it_could_fail: The tile-block halves of Ai2's test splits are mild shifts, so the grade is mostly in-distribution and P3 may be underpowered; that limits the claim to 'graded under mild shift'. Segmentation tasks are imbalanced (sen1floods11 water share small), Deng 2023's declared failure mode for dispersity-based scores; ATC is threshold-based and less exposed, but a per-class version needs full probability vectors the exports lack. If P2 fails in the other direction (naive overestimates), p1 is underconfident on those probes and the failure-mode text must be rewritten.

proposals.name: Run the model-assisted arm exp78 planned and never ran, as PPI++ with a per-stratum tuned coefficient, cross-fitted by tile with design-aware intervals; correct the record where the arm is described as run
field_rules_followed: Angelopoulos, Duchi, Zrnic PPI++: data-tuned lambda, never wider than labelled-only
Fisch et al. StratPPI: lambda per stratum
Kluger et al. 2025: design-aware bootstrap for clustered labelled samples
Mozer 2026 (known): PPI = difference estimator
Audit-before-record (user's rule): an unrun arm must not be described as run
proposals.what_changes: exp78's run_designs gains E3d (lambda = 1, the planned arm), E3d++ (lambda tuned, PPI++), and E3s (lambda per margin quintile, StratPPI), predictor g = 1 - p1 or the ATC-calibrated g from proposal 4, cross-fitted by tile; on the D4 tile design the interval is Kluger's design-aware bootstrap. `estimate` gains `--model-assisted` that uses the predictions on the unlabelled units. The digest sentence 'a difference estimator with confidence as predictor was an arm' and any docs echo are corrected to 'planned in docs/plan/map_error_estimation.md, not run in exp78'.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: A narrower interval from the same 300 labels, guaranteed no wider than the classical one; and a record that says what was run.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes weakly: the user gains precision, not a new kind of statement; ranked below the deliverables above for that reason.
proposals.filter_2_audit_scope: Passes: labels feed an estimator; predictions are auxiliary.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Bounded by the record: exp78 P4 caps any saving at 1.8x against SRS and the capture-based ceiling is 1.66x; with a median margin AUROC of 0.76 the residual err - g keeps most of the variance, so the expected gain over D2c is small and the preregistration says so.
proposals.already_in_record: docs/plan/map_error_estimation.md lists E3d; exp78_summary.json has no E3d key and exp/exp78_error_rate_estimation.py run_designs has no such arm; the guard against fitting the predictor on the sample without cross-fitting is in the plan's invalidation list. Not a repeat: never run.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Estimand: theta per (task, encoder) at B = 300, R = 2000, the exp78 harness. P1 (honesty): coverage >= 0.93 on every cell for E3d++ and E3s (exp78 P1 bar; exp79 P5 tolerance). P2 (guarantee): E3d++ half-width ratio against D2c/E1 <= 1.00 on every cell; a ratio above 1.00 anywhere is a bug in lambda tuning, not a finding. P3 (gain): median ratio across the 7 segmentation tasks <= 0.95 for E3s; if the median is above 0.98 the arm is recorded as 'no gain at this ranking quality' and not shipped as a flag. P4 (why lambda is tuned): plain E3d (lambda = 1) is wider than D2c on at least 2 of 7 tasks. P5 (honesty, exp78 P4): no arm saves more than 1.8x labels against D1/E1 at equal half-width; a larger saving means leakage (predictor fitted on the sample) and P1 is where it shows. P6 (tiles): on the D4 design the i.i.d. PPI interval covers below 0.85 on the task with the largest design effect (MADOS, 9.77) while the design-aware bootstrap covers at 0.93.
proposals.how_it_could_fail: If g = 1 - p1 is uncalibrated, lambda tunes toward 0 and the arm reproduces D2c exactly: honest but empty, and the run still corrects the record. Cross-fitting by tile on classification tasks (no tiles) falls back to random folds, which is fine for D1/D2 but the D4 clause is segmentation-only.

proposals.name: A review set with a guarantee: conformal risk control on the margin so the missed-error rate among unreviewed windows is at most alpha, calibrated on the `sample` labels
field_rules_followed: Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, Schuster ICLR 2024: conformal risk control for a monotone risk, tight to O(1/n)
Learn then Test 2025: high-probability version for non-monotone or stricter guarantees
Li et al. 2026 conformal SAR flood (known)
CEOS 2025: local quality statements beside global ones
proposals.what_changes: `assess --alpha 0.04` returns the margin threshold tau and the review fraction such that the expected missed-error rate among windows above tau is at most alpha, calibrated on the labelled sample `sample` already produces (n = 300), with the exchangeability condition printed (calibration must be an SRS of windows, or a tile draw with a design-effect-inflated n). Grading on every (task, encoder) export: 2000 calibration draws, realised risk on the rest.
proposals.what_a_map_user_gains: An operating point chosen in advance with a stated bound ('review these 12% and at most 4% of what remains is wrong') instead of learning the capture afterwards.
proposals.filter_1_map_user: Passes: how far to trust the unreviewed remainder is a guarantee the tool does not give today.
proposals.filter_2_audit_scope: Passes: the same small labelled sample; no head, no training.
proposals.filter_3_headroom: Not a ranker; it wraps the margin's existing ranking in a bound. Its usefulness is limited by the same capture curves (exp70) that bound the margin.
proposals.already_in_record: exp70 capture at 5/10/20% and exp35 operating points (null) grade fixed budgets after the fact; exp78's sample is the calibration set. Not a repeat: no threshold with a risk bound exists.
proposals.preregistration_sketch: Risk R(tau) = P(error and margin > tau) over unreviewed windows; alpha = half the task's true error rate so 'review halves the residual error'. P1 (guarantee): mean realised R over 2000 SRS calibration draws of n = 300 <= alpha + 1/300 on every cell. P2 (review cost): the review fraction for that alpha is <= 20% on tasks whose exp70 capture at 20% is >= 0.5 (m_eurosat 0.86, mados 0.50 at 10%, sen1floods11 0.46 at 10%) and > 40% on pastis_sentinel1, m_cashew_plant and m_forestnet (capture at 10% <= 0.22). P3 (exchangeability): with tile-clustered calibration draws (16 windows per tile, exp78 D4) the realised mean R exceeds alpha by more than 0.01 on the cell with the largest design effect (MADOS, 9.77) unless n is deflated by the design effect. P4 (conditional honesty): the share of single calibration draws whose realised R exceeds alpha is between 0.4 and 0.6 (the CRC guarantee is in expectation); the tool prints this, and LTT's high-probability tau is reported as the alternative with its extra review cost.
proposals.how_it_could_fail: A user with one calibration sample gets an in-expectation guarantee that misses alpha on about half of draws; if P4 shows the miss is large in magnitude on high-error tasks, the deliverable must ship LTT's version or not ship. Segmentation exchangeability requires the calibration windows to be sampled from the same map, so the guarantee is per map, never transferable across dates, and the docs must say so.

Probe hyperparameter and input-normalisation sensitivity (Lee 2023): the audited claim is about a given probe's own confidence; a re-normalised probe is a different model with different errors and does not test it.
Joint OOD + error DS-AURC grading (Li 2026): no out-of-support stratum exists in Ai2's suite.
ConfIC-RCA per-map segmentation quality (Cosarinsky 2025): needs an in-context segmenter, a new model, which filter 2 forbids as a deliverable.

Embedding-geometry diagnostics, per-dimension probe reliance and ERA5 covariate probing (Rahman 2026, Benavides-Martinez 2026, Mocharla & Patel 2026): no route to a statement a map user acts on, and exp73/exp77 say feature-space statistics carry no error information here.
Temporal-window sensitivity (Guerrero-Viu 2026): single-date encoders throughout.
Blind double-interpreter validation (Mughees 2026): a label-collection project, not a methodology change; its output (reviewer error rate) enters proposal 1 as a stated band instead.

Active statistical inference and robust mixing (Zrnic & Candes 2024; Li, Zrnic, Candes 2025): exp78's D2c already sits within 0.0007 half-width of the oracle allocation D2star, so the allocation has no headroom for an active rule to claim.

Label-free score aggregation of the margin with a second cue (Steinmetz 2026): it is another ranker; exp65's label-fitted fusion gained 0.0006 and the label-free midrank fusion is already a recorded loss (claim label-free-midrank-fusion-lost).

Controlled label-flip sensitivity of E-AURC (Nogueira 2026, Foody 2024): random flips do not model reference error, which exp23 shows is spatially structured (10.8% of errors vs 0.8% of correct windows changed class); kept as the reviewer-error band in proposal 1.

FALCON false-confidence concentration statistic (Cenacchi 2026): needs the cached bank for compactness, its ingredients each lost in exp73, and its spatial analogue is already exp78's design effect (1.2-9.8).
Active or planted-slice region verification (Zhang 2025; Domino, Spotlight, SpotCheck, MCSD): the tool ships no region-discovery deliverable; reliability.kmeans has no callers in the package.
HiBug2 attribute-conjunction enumeration as its own proposal: with three cues computable from the exports the conjunction table has seven cells; folded into proposal 2 (P4).
Family-wise multiplicity control as its own proposal: Holm changes no recorded verdict (smallest p 1.1e-4 against a bar of 0.0026); folded into proposal 3 as one line.
Task-subset resampling against the benchmark lottery (Dehghani 2021): the claims are per-task win counts, and any subset of a 24/24 result is all wins; no information.
Calibration grade (ECE) of the margin per task: one number a map user cannot act on; it matters only where the margin is used as a probability, which proposal 4 grades directly by MAE.
Target-weighted cross-validation (Brenning & Suesse 2026): `estimate` samples the deployment map itself, so validation-to-deployment reweighting does not arise.
